The importance of the 2026 election is obvious. A dictatorial president subverting the constitution to gain more power for himself while Congress stands by in thrall, subservient to his political movement. November may be our last chance to stand and defend our democracy and our elections.
Pitch in $35 -- right now -- to fuel our efforts to inform eligible voters, get them registered, get their ballot cast, and make every vote count >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=061826_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]

It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

subject: I will shut down Pete Hegseth’s incompetent reign of terror.

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
Let me be frank about something. I am a Black man born and raised in rural Louisiana. As a third generation farmer, my son and I work the same Delta land that my granddad worked as a sharecropper—except now we own it.
What I am trying to say is: I can smell racist BS from miles away. And right now, Pete Hegseth’s Defense Department stinks to high heaven.
Pete Hegseth is playing favorites and passing over qualified Black and female servicemembers for promotions, and targeting them for demotion and dismissal—while also promoting inexperienced MAGA loyalists.
Nearly 60 percent of the senior officers fired by Hegseth are female or Black. Women and racial minorities in our military have been denied promotions, baselessly fired or dismissed, or have been pushed out of the ranks at alarming and unprecedented rates.
Rewarding loyalty to MAGA above the experience, expertise, and exemplary service of the men and women who have dedicated their lives to our country is both despicable and dangerous.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
This isn’t about DEI, racial equity, or even just basic human decency: Pete Hegseth’s unsteady, bigoted, and dangerous leadership of the Department of Defense is putting every single one of us at risk.
Hegseth has unraveled the merit-based system that kept our military strong for generations. He’s turning our military into a MAGA loyalty clown show.
I pledge to you: When I am elected to the United States Senate, I will make it my personal mission to shut this foolishness down and get back to putting experienced personnel in the positions that matter most .
I am Jamie Davis, a third-generation family farmer running to defeat MAGA extremism in this wide open US Senate seat in Louisiana. Together we can make history, flip this seat, and reclaim the US Senate for Democrats. Will you make a donation of $15, $25 or any amount to help me and my team pull off an upset victory this midterm election? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
HELP ELECT A REAL WORKING-CLASS CHAMPION TO THE SENATE! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
Thank you. Your support means more than you know.
Jamie Davis
Democrat for US Senate
Louisiana

subject: The threat of AI job losses

body:
Peter, we must prepare our workers for the changing economy.
Hello Peter,We are living through a period of rapid technological change, and while innovation can bring great benefits, it also brings real disruptions to our workforce.**Recently, in just one single month, six companies closed their facilities in Wisconsin, costing nearly 1,000 of our neighbors their jobs. Across our country, thousands of workers are facing layoffs due to the impact of automation and AI.** This is a crisis that we cannot ignore. If we do not act, our workforce and our communities will be left behind.As a former senior leader in the Department of Workforce Development, I know that we must proactively prepare our workforce for the jobs of tomorrow.**Instead of waiting for layoffs to happen, we must:**
* Expand pre-apprenticeship and technical training programs to help workers transition into high-skill, family-supporting careers.
* Partner with our world-class Wisconsin technical colleges and the private sector to align training with real, available jobs.
* Create incentives for businesses to upskill their current workers rather than replacing them.

When I was at the Department of Workforce Development, I led an effort to quickly review, approve, and contract a public-private grant to help hundreds of Wisconsinites enter pre-apprenticeship training for construction trades. That's the kind of speed and decisiveness we need to protect our workers.We can protect Wisconsin jobs and make our state a leader in the modern economy.**Please consider supporting our campaign today so we can bring this critical, forward-looking leadership to Madison.**[**[PROTECT WISCONSIN JOBS ➔]**](https://willmartinforltgovernor.cmail20.com/t/j-l-ydkhwdk-hkjudtlhit-r/)Thank you for your partnership.Warmly,Will Martin

subject: It’s not time to panic… yet
body:

Derek — our end-of-quarter deadline is in just a couple of weeks. Once it passes, we’ll be required to report how much we’ve raised in Q2, and _everyone_ will be looking at that number. **The truth is that we _need_ to report a strong fundraising total.** Not just to show that we have strong support behind us, but because we absolutely have to hit our fundraising goals to ensure that Democrats have the resources that they need to run winning campaigns this year. Right now, we’re pacing to fall short of our goal, **_but we’re not panicking yet.**_ We’re going to need a massive influx of grassroots contributions to finish strong, Derek. And if every person receiving this email chipped in $7, _we’d blow our end-of-quarter goal out of the water._ But the unfortunate truth is that most people won’t even open this email, let alone give. | Roughly 2.1 million Americans identify as transgender.
---

We love having you in our network, but if you'd like to unsubscribe,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=1&akid=2528%2E259176%2EhVWg8m)_

They are our neighbors, siblings, friends, parents, and spouses. They work hard to support themselves and their families. Some have also chosen to serve our great nation in the military; in local, state, and federal government; and in other leadership positions. On day one of his second term, President Trump signed an executive order to **remove all trans people from military service.** Trans adults nationwide have lost access to medical treatment or even had treatments canceled because hospitals and clinics have been forced to roll back gender-affirming care under Trump. **It’s clear that transgender Americans have become a scapegoat for the GOP. We must stand up for our neighbors and speak out against these discriminatory policies._[Sign on now to show your support for trans rights in the United States!](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/13752?source=LOC_EM_PET_2026.06.18_OG-Trans-Rights_B5_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_N-T0&t=3&akid=2528%2E259176%2EhVWg8m)_** | [SIGN ON NOW →](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/13752?source=LOC_EM_PET_2026.06.18_OG-Trans-Rights_B5_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_N-T0&t=4&akid=2528%2E259176%2EhVWg8m)

name: Barlow For Wyo
subject: Barlow For Wyoming Newsletter
body:
Special Forum Edition
| | | | | | [ ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KVEXANVE9Z36AJ738N05YM2Y_0)
---
| **Welcome to the Barlow for Wyoming Newsletter. Your hub for latest news, information and upcoming events.**
---
|
---
| | |
---
| Hi Friends,When I decided to run for Governor, I told my campaign team to look for opportunities where I could join other gubernatorial candidates to discuss the issues facing Wyoming and dive in deeper than just top-line messaging. I am so thankful to the many organizations across the state that have stepped up to host forums and debates. Unfortunately, we can't attend all of them. But I am trying to make as many as feasible and ensure I cover as broad a range of topics as possible.I have appreciated each of these conversations. The questions have been thoughtful, practical, and rooted in the real work happening across Wyoming every day. So far, we have talked about our legacy and future extractive energy industries, healthcare, education, taxes, local government, economic development, families, and the future of our communities.These forums are important because they give Wyoming voters the chance to hear directly from candidates and think through the kind of leadership our state needs.For Kelly and me, they have also been a reminder of why we are in this race: to listen, work hard, and stay focused on Wyoming solutions for Wyoming problems. I am not running against anyone, I am running for Wyoming which hopefully is evident in how I show up at these events.
* After tonight's Wyoming Republican Party debate, I will have met other candidates at 7 forums with at least 4 more planned. Below is a list of past and upcoming forums including the names of the host organizations.
* May 11, Petroleum Association of Wyoming (Casper)
* June 4, Wyoming Mining Association (Gillette)
* June 5, Wyoming Association of Municipalities (Laramie)
* June 5, Greater Cheyenne Chamber of Commerce (Cheyenne) -- forum recording below
* June 9, Wyoming Family Conservative Candidate Forum presented by the Wyoming Family Alliance (Cheyenne) -- forum recording below
* June 12, Wyoming Healthcare Policy Summit presented by the Wyoming Medical Society, Wyoming Hospital Association, Wyoming Nurses Association, and Wyoming Primary Care Association (Laramie) -- forum recording below
* June 18 at 7:30pm, Wyoming Republican Party (Dubois) -- watch it live or recorded later [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y805InM6ArI](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KVEXANVE9Z36AJ738N05YM2Y_1)
* June 23, Gubernatorial Candidate Agriculture Forum Breakfast presented by the Wyoming Farm Bureau Federation, Wyoming Stock Growers Association, and Wyoming Wool Growers Association (Casper)
* July 22, League of Women Voters, WyoFile, and Wyoming Public Radio Gubernoatorial Forum (Casper)
* July 30, The 2026 WCSP Gubernatorial Forum presented by Wyoming Community Service Providers, Natrona Collective Health Trust, Wyoming Governor’s Council on Developmental Disabilities, Wyoming Independent Living, and Child Development Center
* August 6, The 2026 Gubernatorial Debate presented by Wyoming PBS, Wyoming Public Media, and Cowboy State Daily

Not all forums were streamed or recorded, but several were. I encourage you to watch and share with your friends, especially those who you are reminding to vote in the upcoming primary. Watch the campaign social media sites and newsletters for reminders and links to upcoming events.See you on the trail!\- Eric
---
| | [ SUPPORT ERIC! ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KVEXANVE9Z36AJ738N05YM2Y_2)
---
|
---
| **FORUM POSTS FROM FACEBOOK**
---
| **WYOMING HEALTHCARE POLICY SUMMIT** I appreciated being asked to join the forum at the Wyoming Healthcare Policy Summit in Laramie. I’ve watched many in that were in the room make improvements and serve Wyoming citizens for years, even as things have gotten tougher, but there is still a lot of work to do. Let's keep going.
---
| | [ Watch the Healthcare Forum Replay ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KVEXANVE9Z36AJ738N05YM2Y_3)
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
|
---
| **WYOMING FAMILY ALLIANCE** I participated in the Wyoming Family Alliance forum in Cheyenne, and it was a fruitful discussion about what Wyoming families need. Kelly and I believe Wyoming families are the foundation of everything we are fighting for. Parents deserve a real voice in their children’s education. Communities deserve local control. And every child in Wyoming deserves the opportunity to get a meaningful education, raise a family, and build a life right here at home. We are pro-life, and we back that up with support for maternal health, community-based care, and resources for women and children across Wyoming.

When they do this, there will be nothing standing in the way of every Republican Governor in America purging their registered voters list on Monday, November 2nd, the day before the election and removing every registered Democratic voter from their rolls.

## Robin Hood's Legendary Tree Dies
The [Major Oak in Sherwood Forest](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ8GOke7tjFQuPibdPnbK5GDl7B3DotsKxFvfyKvcPVI8803X7fpFjjx9vgfnuTrItNG75KoVsqTcFqSvEuWO2-rSCw1E0WmSYN2CpzCcYqB0zHZNvqFSJNpyWM_4ODMoF27-uhcXLAzTsM8UOxCIDM4u3T9ON5xNi37sw0cjggI2l6snTtjgpnRAmDoGwsUuUq-fAtvdaUlHfKifJnl2Sa_1rqXxvxr9LXR151kT3RGjb6GbWbaqpLwo87p6mOiThUVmYpCpQHUQSEXhRoAu35ss4_7m1Pi4k724xk4fVj1Twe9vP4NAAD__xTpeKM), the 1,200-year-old tree that legend says sheltered Robin Hood inside its hollow trunk, is believed to have died after failing to produce leaves this spring. The Royal Society for the Protection of Birds said centuries of visitors [compacted the soil](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAURb8Gd1iAHWwXFJFWlrbIdqsprWd4xG-EIQImnvz9yPmFqa_u1Tn347bcgALF-z_Y0VSflohHCVgr5iVR8CEdJaeV4paSKzUjOsJFCaW50FxOiwMKr6VvnPGICrsGjRxGOepuVLrZzDpKDWIaJg9y7eQA4NCOdhW9t0L7tSFzrgktJymkUH3b9_bSddBZ2QshYWC9QEc15fYzUawb-vBKT8ytTXsTzFbro7DuytTM1HwcR7uXeGZMzRg5fDE17ynii6n5jhEzBKZmiJYwVv5246ccP-U4Fe4QHMfvB-ZaeIGzB5lfr-ry_y_8abJxj4NCoKJPtPsOFN4o9Vf_PY36CQAA__96T4Us) around the massive oak until it was as hard as concrete, strangling the root system and cutting off water and nutrients. The tree had been fenced off since the 1970s, but the damage was already deep. Metal bracing, concrete fills, and structural props meant to save the tree likely made things worse, preventing it from aging naturally. Recent heatwaves and drought compounded the decline. The oak will remain standing as a wildlife habitat and monument, and saplings from the tree have been planted around the world. A Hugh Jackman film, _The Death of Robin Hood_ , opens Friday. ## Supreme Court Sides with Texas Man
The U.S. Supreme Court [ruled unanimously on Thursday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGyozAMBdCvMZ0Y2_hBKCi2oXvbbsnIIIL3gZ2x5JD8_Q75hW3UaOaeO_fP9_SNYQ_x_hsPGuS1pinSyTuJUJ6Kp5yTT4KvwCFuqbCkuOLPZLVtQbdg-mnBsL8nVy2D10tvKhpMdzO3ttO2q7ahX13XmC_C1vXOz7r3XafRzx5bcq7zVRiuMN2a3hjdOFc33n0tfeublXqjG1JO0xIk5Vo2Enohr_s7PSnXczqqfdhEHqyaX8qOyo7nedY_jHI9lR194RCJWdnxYpQd9XXMTdmRyyPTQTCnkgU4LMRwBtkA4cPAgRHOLQHjmyEIQ0wCCHMOB8GaMhyYw9-CEaEwZQZJsOGT4F7iJVZ5WB5n2PfAbaecvh8Y9k9r-b-tn4P9FwAA___WlpVR) that the government cannot strip a Texas man of his guns because he uses marijuana. The decision in _U.S. v. Hemani_ favored Ali Danial Hemani, charged under a 1968 law after FBI agents [found a handgun and marijuana](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD0TnCAYhH-NdjiAiFJQpLG7tCkdPl71zSE4gOfdv89cyrQpd3ZmZ5_n12N5GAwYt5_mAF3fa1oi3CVArZCXy0LOyaZq3lgw7ukqNcXVPBdOuSRUEqYWbzB8FtF6balXrAXNxolNcqR8bHc9gBiHwYMRSspxGDll1FnB5eAnJenUov6OUckUY7QXouutGLyStl9BMdpDIyh4rCl3dYcKb1PW8EkvyJ1LRxv0XutZmv5Hw-eGz_d9d9G6L8W3b_h8poAVXWn4XK4zwwHEpSvXfzOxxj0LOUzG35eJhlwFciFuNyFA3IBkKDWjq5gi2a5I0h0hlx1JdtFwKVXP2qz9eWMIWOTYCLodBsPfn_X_7L40_xMAAP__9NmSgQ) at his Texas home. He faced no other charges and wasn't accused of being armed while high. Writing for the court, [Justice Neil Gorsuch said](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL0O3CAQhJ8Gd1gsJjYuKNK4u7QpLTCLjYLhxM_57u0jn5QnSLVajebTzPx-rA_tg4_7L32iqm-X1ohXCVgr5rUZzDmZVPXbFx-P1EpN0ek_K2d8pGykMK9W-_BZRWeVYXaGDhVMEuQ4MT51h9qsQ0AjQcIouZA4owQEdJMYGHDXeXXD2AgzABuE6Acjfth5NIPDGdiARDC0vqbc1wMrvnVx4ZNemPstnV1QR63PQoafhC-EL9d19dFs1l23TPhy97mPrj5FHaiPFfO_j_CltGfGE-mWWq70y6ebLkiDvqjNbaetYC50b5Ee7TZT4y1GwhfBBgmzIHzpsrLPy4fgyzgRwfZT-_DNV_9v1ZfifwMAAP__m2GOeQ) the government can't treat everyone who regularly uses marijuana as "categorically violent and dangerous." The narrow ruling leaves the underlying ban intact and marked a loss for the Trump administration, which defended it. The case drew unusual allies. The ACLU and the National Rifle Association backed Hemani, while gun-control group Everytown and the Justice Department argued that habitual drug users pose a danger that justifies the ban. Gorsuch said the [government hadn't met](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O6yAUhJ8Gd1gcTHBcUNzGXW67pQXmYKPFJuInJG-_8r7CdiONNKPv-3osD-2DP7f_-kBV3i4uJ7YcsBRMSzWYUjSx6LfP_txjzSWeTn8vnHFJmaQwLVb78FlEZ5VhdoIOFYx3uMuR8bHbFVhcjZAcHLsZAULgzTkBd7Y6sIPknVfXGJMwAbBBiH4w4mYnaQaHE7ABiWBofYmpLzsWfOvswie-MPVrPLqg9lKemQz_CJ8Jn1tr_WryRXH1hM9XJHzO9ZnwQLrGmgq1qW60ZkyZbvWkQTdaM33RHQ99esLnLin7bD4En-VIBNsO7cPvY_mbp5fiPwEAAP__Yzd-iA) its burden to prove that.
## Texas Weighs Data-Center Grid Rules
Texas energy regulators are [close to approving](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2uozAUBOCnMZ0j_12DCxfb0N1tt0QHfCDWdWzWPpDw9qvkFbYbaaRPo_nzPX1DTDFvv-GBnl5rmTI-W0IirNMxY61lLgSv2GK-l6NRySv8TEooy4Xl0k0BYrom0wU_i-Bkh172gxxsL1Tf3b1UMCxhCFYK6_rByGVAF76MctL2EtYu-jcmrHRSCm3MTc_mKzg76xWdFBqZERgilXqjOxK-oK3pKifW21IeXfJ3or0x_YupkakR5kXqd8PU2KjUi6kxAAFfMBPWxhviDyfY-YfimLFuF6-4HQmo1MahIl9Sachh32s5Y954xic_keidK_49sFFjapROK6WtYGrsqg_7M6YUm-2ZEdsDYvospP_79fTqXwAAAP__uzyOdA) a new way to screen data centers flooding the grid with connection requests. The Public Utility Commission was set to vote yesterday on an ERCOT plan to [study data-center hookups in groups](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGupCAYBeCnwQ4DiAoFxTZ2d9stDcivkmFgAr-j8_Yb5xVuc5qTfDk5_37mHxtiSNtf-wSD15rnBGeNgAhlPhyUkl1Ge4Ua0p6Pijmt9jELJgbKBsr17G2In1k23jjmNW_A8FFxNYxMjM1uBrUq6P3qe67A9tqOzjvdA_OsV9LLJpgbYwPXnLNOyrZzsvd6cN0KmrMOiGTgA-bS4g4Il61r_OQ3lHbJzyaaHfFVSfeHiImI6TzP9uHwuksiptsmYmJ3cEXE9AVozPlRKYZtR0i0HBEq9RYtXSAhlEpxhw-NIQE9XnTJKcGCFMqSkW4leCKmphj_OkOMoQ4jkWx72hC_k_B3R76N-B8AAP__iaWI6g), or "batches," rather than one at a time. ERCOT says its old system, built for 40 to 50 large projects, was swamped by 225 requests last year, about 70% of them data centers. The first round, "Batch Zero," would screen only projects that have already locked in land and financing, separating serious proposals from speculative "paper" ones. Supporters say the change protects grid reliability, while some residents worry about the strain on power, water, and neighborhoods. The overhaul follows a [directive this month](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2S4yAQhJ9GylDxIyMREFzibC-9UDWCwaIOMy4Yeb1vf-W9R9i4u77q_v58bB-QS66333BHz69EW8XPXpAZ23bu2BrtxPDKPdeDzs5UE_zdtNRWSCuU2yLk8rXNY_S7jE6N6NWyqtUuUi_j4a2BOZl0kWCNc5D0uhoDaokurHNUlzH7N0xa5ZSSZp4ns8-X6OxuEjolDQ6zxJiZ2sQHMr6gp_JFT2xToPtY_MH86IP5NejroK83ek7fpelGz0Ff33cGfX1Q5_8ptkpNwL4Ts4i5YeAuHmcQUKPAFogFk-hHxhLFm1S7SI3uIgKDCFgZm8g1NejczsBnQxGocx-bj4_PXErudhlmebtDLt8b-Wdmn17_CwAA__808ZH8) from Gov. Greg Abbott, who told regulators to make data centers pay for their own grid upgrades and to keep those costs off residential bills.
## Uber's Lucid Robotaxis Coming to Houston
Uber, Lucid, and Nuro [have named Houston](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2SrCAQBeCnwUwLEHEICG5iNjfd0EJox65FmMJmft5-y63dJ9i8q8_5zsd1vjqMmG7_3Q6WXmueEzyPCERQ5rpAKXnJ5F54YNpyPSin1X3Okkvdct0KMweH8T2rJtiFByMasGK8iIseuRybzSoV1mXogwCjgwkOxkGC9wG8H6RwvEF7PuNaGCF4r1TXL2oIRi_9CkbwHpjiEJBy6WgDgpc71vjODyidz3sT7UZ0P1j_j8mJyemnZOdrpFpgd_fzjMnpdDE5YUr54QhzYnI6gW2qJbexegztL7aNria_MTk1xYb7E2PEQ49M8dvuMH4H09_melj5FQAA__80SIKf) as the second market for their autonomous [robotaxi program](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHO2yAUhZ_G3m50wRjCwNAl29-1owXhOkYlEMFN4vTpK1ftE3Q5y5GOvu_8-Fq-fMqp3L77Ozne17oUevdMzNSWZ6DWaqjs99RT2eqzcy2r_7lIlBpQg7BL9Cl_FjVGFzBaMZIT5izO2qA04-YwijOuaKKe7BzMrPx1phCiMjaQVnZM7hhDLawQOCl1moKao9VhWskKnGhQSDFxbSfeiGn3fc2f-qJ2utb7mN3G_OjD9G2Ql0FebunXvcZ6dIO8_EWGN8HmXwQe_vnAIQepA-0PX2IqN-jUXulKwBV4I8i1EHT27QgmKLQzfMg3kIhozISzGpuLj3fKOXVtBoW3u0_5Dxf_35svJ38HAAD__zDEi74), with service launching by mid-2027 exclusively through the Uber app. The service will launch first in the San Francisco Bay Area later this year. The fleet will use [Lucid Gravity SUVs](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uhDAQhJ8GOtDaBnMuXKShu7Qp0Rovh3UGn-zlft4-Iq-QZvQVo9HM_FynK4YY9ts3bmT5vaRpp1eJxEx5OhzlnFxifIcS9jUdhdO-4H2SIHUDuhFm8hjiZ-pqbx14I2qyYriIix5ADvVqFele0TJ7BVIZB4ugGXowg0Jw2mEd7BkGWhghQHVdq1zXe6OdWsgIUFR1QD5wyi2vxPTGssRPelJu57TV0a7Mj1Kpr0qOlRyXsOM-U_vBNaXTUclxw3wnLpUcC6f5fgJmDnOkE-MxB9_EU5hwK805u9mPnBqhhVH9pevblbdYZ-sfrxBjKHqoOrhtGOJfCf7fdU8rfwMAAP__hDKEEg) running Nuro's Level 4 self-driving platform, paired with cameras, lidar, radar, and a roof-mounted "halo." Nuro is already road-testing nearly 100 vehicles, with safety operators, across California and Texas. body:
Hi Peter,

We are excited to invite you to the Fond du Lac Labor Temple on Monday,
June 22, at 6:00 PM for a conversation with Mike and MASH President Peter
Rickman about the growing power of corporate monopolies, price gouging, and
the fight to raise the minimum wage in Wisconsin and across the country.

At a time when working families are being squeezed by rising costs and
corporate greed, we'll discuss what can be done to build an economy that
works for everyone—not just those at the top. Because if you work 40 hours
a week, you should be able to afford a roof over your head, put food on the
table, and provide for your family with dignity.

We hope you'll join us for this important discussion and help be part of
the movement for a fairer economy and stronger communities.

Sign-up with the flyer below, RSVP's encouraged but not necessary!

Mike Thurow

name: Teichert in the Trenches
subject: Home Run Communication
body:
One of our favorite family text chains took...
---
| | | | | |
---
| | 💥Home Run Communication💥
---
One of our favorite family text chains took place nearly a year ago when we dropped off Noah at Vanderbilt. Melonie and I were back at our hotel, and Noah was getting situated in his dorm. Via text, we decided when and where we would meet up later.
Noah: “Ballpark 3:50 good?”
Me: “Yes”
The information was communicated and received! Or was it? Several hours later ...
Noah: “Where are y’all”
Me: “We are about 10 minutes away from the ballpark”
Noah: “So where are we meeting?”
Me: “The ballpark?”
Noah: “The ballpark? Why?”
Me: “That’s what you said above – 3:50 at the ballpark”
Noah: “Wait are you serious”
Me: “Yes”
Noah: “I meant ballpark, like I’d be done around then. Not literally at the ballpark.”
We found ourselves swinging and missing. It was a clear FAIL!
We still get a pretty good laugh about it as a family. And of course, Mel and I made our way to the ballpark the next day to snap a bunch of pictures that we used throughout the year anytime Noah needed a pick-me-up. The ballpark is now our favorite place on campus.
Yet, the text chain was a great example of failed communication. It was a complete strike out, and Noah and I were both to blame.
We are told that clear, concise, correct, and complete are the attributes of successful communication. And it is a two-way street. Communication transmitted is not necessarily communication received.
All of these concepts are valid, and nowhere is this concept more critical than in leadership.
It’s easy to shrug off poor performance as the fault of the subordinate. But often, that isn’t the whole picture. In fact, leadership experts say that 80 to 90 percent of the time a subordinate falls short it’s the fault of the leader due to lack of communication that fails to set clear expectations and provide regular feedback.
Shortcomings provide a leader the motivation to step out of the batter’s box and consider the following thoughts (these concepts parallel my post about Dominance Through Debriefs from April):

* Did you give your subordinate clear, concise, correct, complete expectations from day one?
* Written ones provide an ideal way to ensure that the communication is precise for both the leader and the subordinate.

* In delivering expectations, did you ensure that the session allowed for clarification and iteration?

* In delivering the expectations, did you explain your intent, your vision, and your overarching objectives to allow a subordinate the freedom to create and innovate to achieve them?
* With properly-explained intent, you’ll often find that a subordinate will deliver a far better result than you could even imagine.

* Did you follow along with enough fidelity and regularity to understand how things were going?
* Trust but verify, and PLEASE avoid sapping initiative through micromanagement

* Do you provide an environment with regular opportunities for feedback to highlight successes, offer resources, seek opportunities to break down barriers, and redirect when needed to steer away from shortcomings?
* Semi-annual and annual feedback is not sufficient. Just imagine if I bottled up my feedback to my kids while they were growing up for the next annual performance review. It would be parental neglect. Similarly, it’s leadership neglect in the workplace.
* When giving feedback about shortcomings, seek to find the root cause of any problems.

* During your feedback sessions, do you refer back to your original expectations?
* If needed, use your feedback sessions to update expectations.

Confusing communication is all around us, and it’s causing our organizations to strike out in accomplishing their mission. Many times, we aren’t even in the ballpark of clear, concise, correct, and complete. Yet, carefully applying the concepts of communication will help you LEAD WELL! It will be a home run for your organization, your team, and your mission.

* John

| Fellow Patriot,

Ron Eller won the Republican primary.

And before the votes were even fully counted, the Democrat machine and Bennie Thompson were already making moves.

That is how much they want to keep this seat. Democrats in Congress know that if they lose Bennie Thompson's seat, they can't take back the House from Republicans. He has unlimited dark money, out-of-state donors, and a playbook designed to defeat Ron before November.

Here is what they are up against.

Ron is medical professional who has worked throughout central Mississippi. He is a former U.S. Army officer, small business owner, and supported by President Trump. He's against tax increases, wants to balance the federal budget, is the state leader of the term limits movement, protect our borders, and kick out the violent criminals and drug traffickers threatening our families.

President Trump has had enough of Bennie Thompson, and he knows he can count on Ron Eller's support in DC.

But none of that matters if we can't match the Democrats’ fundraising machine in this race.

Right now we need to show the country that Mississippi grassroots conservatives are ready to fight. A strong fundraising number this month tells Bennie Thompson and the DC Democrats that Mississippi is not for sale.

Will you chip in $10, $25, or whatever you can today to help Ron take on the Democrat machine this fall?

This is the race that could decide the House majority. Ron is the candidate who can win it.

Let's get to work.

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

**FROM:** Cait Conley for NY-17
**MEMO:** Tonight's Deadline **** **_NY-17 is one of only three districts nationwide that split their ticket in 2024 for Kamala Harris and a Republican member of Congress._** Mike Lawler is beatable. This is a winnable district. But we need to be ready for a tough fight. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | $7M+ Revenue 1.5M users. name: Wes Moore
subject: Happy Juneteenth, Peter
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1516%2E1086043%2EhsLj2L)
Happy Juneteenth, Peter.
Today, we celebrate the moment the last enslaved Americans finally heard the words: you are free.
Juneteenth is a beautiful reckoning, but also a reminder that our work isn't done.
As governor, I've fought to make that freedom real every day — from fighting to close the racial wealth gap by removing barriers to employment, education, and homeownership for thousands of Marylanders, to making history with the largest single mass pardon for cannabis possession in this country.
But there's still more to do. Loving your country doesn't mean lying about its history. **Real patriotism means knowing we can always be better, and doing the work to get there.**
So this Juneteenth, let's honor those who came before us and recommit to the fight for a better future. For every Marylander, everywhere.
Elevate,
Wes

name: Shontel Brown
subject: Juneteenth isn’t just a celebration. It’s a promise.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Shontel Brown for Congress
body:
Today, we observe the 161st anniversary of Juneteenth.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133612310/628481101/-153530995?refcode=EM_C_260619juneteenth_N_SB_90DO_6_NG_N_Logo&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjMjM1YmVkZC1kZTZiLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ny6pzx3xWd2MoNPEGBC8bXiMeWmgs0i_Tk3UdBuQfxg=) Peter,

Today, we observe the 161st anniversary of Juneteenth, celebrating the liberation and resilience of Black Americans. On June 19, 1865, the news of freedom finally reached the last emancipated people in Texas, two and a half years after President Abraham Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation.

**That struggle did not end on Juneteenth.** Freedom has never been simply granted. It has been fought for in courtrooms, classrooms, in churches, and on picket lines. It has been demanded, defended, marched for, and sacrificed for generation after generation. It continued through the iron grip of Jim Crow and segregation. It continued to the ballot box, where Black Americans not only had to fight for their freedom to vote but also for their votes to count equally.

**The ability to vote, be heard, and elect leaders that represent our communities was not a gift. It was victories won through sacrifice. And today, those victories are once again under attack.**

Ideological extremists appointed by Donald Trump on the Supreme Court have shattered the protections we’ve fought so hard for. They continue to chip away at the Voting Rights Act and allow far-right politicians to suppress Black Americans’ votes and dilute our political power. Every generation inherits the responsibility to protect what previous generations sacrificed, and we cannot surrender or give up the fight to defend equal representation.

**Juneteenth isn’t just a celebration. It’s a responsibility and a promise – a promise to defend and protect the freedoms we were first denied.**

There’s no greater honor than fighting for the rights of my people and every disenfranchised American during this pivotal time in our history.

Gratefully,

Shontel Brown | Shontel Brown is proud to be elected as the Congresswoman for Ohio’s 11th District. She has spent the last decade serving the people of Ohio and building coalitions. As she enters her second full term in Congress, she will use that experience to continue the fight for affordable quality health care, jobs that pay fair wages, a strong public education system, and to preserve and protect our democracy for generations to come. Will you join her and be the change we need?

RON HANKS · CONSERVATIVE REPUBLICAN · US HOUSE – DISTRICT 3 · JUNE 30 PRIMARY

** An Appeal to Patriots and Veterans
------------------------------------------------------------

Not for money. For COUNTRY.

It has been an emotional stretch of patriotic holidays—Memorial Day, D-Day, Flag Day—with Independence Day approaching in our nation’s 250th year. I’m grateful President Trump is in charge, but real threats remain at home and abroad.

I served 32 years in the Air Force—enlisted and commissioned, active, reserve, and civilian. More than half my life in uniform. I’m fully vested in this country, yet deeply uneasy. Our government has grown too powerful, operated covertly against its own citizens, wasted our treasure and laundered it for their political benefit. It belonged to our families and children.

Career politicians treat districts like inconveniences while lobbyists and DC insiders pull the strings. They flood our mail with deceptive LIAR FLYERS, dodge town halls, and protect the status quo. My opponent earned an “F” from Heritage Action – his 59% is fully 26 points below the average Republican. Yet his LIAR FLYERS proclaim he is “conservative”.

I’ve done the local interviews my opponent declined. I’ve answered detailed questionnaires with clear positions while he offers bland generics. I seek no endorsements—just your consideration and your vote.

I’m running for Congress as a final tour of duty. My mission: Advance the America First agenda. Support the next conservative President. Return home.

Citizen-soldier, citizen-legislator, citizen again. That’s the model of government and service our Founders established and challenged us to keep.

Vote Ron Hanks, and send me to Washington as a true conservative who will support President Trump.

I am Top Line on the ballot – because I showed up. The other guy didn’t.

We have the greatest system of government in the world, but corruption and waste have overwhelmed it. Fake conservatives won’t fix it...... I will.

Let’s Roll,

Ron Hanks

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: The important things have lost priority
body:
A future where Abbott is governor for 4 more years doesn’t seem right.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
After over a decade of Greg Abbott’s leadership, I need to ask: **_Are we better off?_**
For far too many Texans, the answer is a resounding no. If you want to know what another four years of Greg Abbott will look like:
❌ **Public schools will keep closing.** Thanks to Greg Abbott’s Voucher Scam, more and more neighborhood schools are facing multimillion-dollar deficits and shutting their doors permanently. Under his watch, our teachers are severely underpaid, and school districts are forced to do more with less while taxpayer money is funneled to wealthy private academies.
❌ **Healthcare will remain completely out of reach for some communities.** Greg Abbott continuously refuses to properly fund and expand healthcare, leaving Texas with the highest number of uninsured children in the country. He’s putting immense pressure on local hospitals, clinics, and families who are already drowning in medical expenses.
❌ **Our infrastructure will continue to go ignored.** After multiple failures and repeated warnings about the vulnerability of our energy grid, Abbott’s answer is still thoughts and prayers instead of real preparedness. Texans deserve a reliable grid, not corporate excuses.
With Greg Abbott, big promises to his corporate donors come first, and accountability to everyday Texans comes dead last.
Texans are tired of watching our schools, healthcare, and basic affordability lose priority while he plays corrupt political games just to stay in power. We can’t afford another four years of this failed leadership.
That’s why I’m running for governor — because I’m determined to deliver real results for _all_ Texans.
**[If you believe Texans deserve a real leader who puts working families ahead of special interests, will you chip in $5 today to support my campaign for governor and help us win this November?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260619_1_4years.-KHDhc&refcode=em20260619-1371&amount=5&t=1&akid=1371%2E299639%2EYAoQ4d)**

Thank you,
Gina

Peter, Today, on Juneteenth, we honor the long and ongoing fight for Black liberation and the fundamental right to a voice in our democracy. This week, Georgians can celebrate a major victory for Black voting rights: **Thanks to our massive grassroots response to Gov. Kemp’s proposed redistricting scheme, legislators have abandoned any attempt to redraw our district maps during the current special session.** This is a powerful reminder of what we can accomplish when we organize, fight back, and make our voices heard. Everybody remembers the predator. Almost nobody remembers the people who protected him (99% of the time it's "him"). For profit. For politics. For a promotion. Or for promotional reasons.
That last one is why amoral news-hoarders Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan held onto Epstein stories exposing the Trump Administration's treachery for a year. Sharing these stories may have saved lives. Prevented political catastrophes to come.
But saving these stories scored them a huge book deal! And, c'mon, they're corporate media! They got bank to earn by withholding key information when it could help. I know I read somewhere that was the purpose of a free press being included in the 1st Amendment.
Yes, I could go on ripping these nepo-cretins further. But how about we let the Epstein survivors, who released a statement in response "journalists" turning news tricks, do the talking here:
> Today, on behalf of survivors of Jeffrey Epstein's abuse and trafficking network, we are responding to the release of Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan's book and the reported inclusion of disturbing Epstein-related information that was not made public when it was first known. For survivors, this is not about politics, media competition, publishing, or book sales. This is about justice. Information connected to Jeffrey Epstein, his associates, the people who enabled him, and the institutions that protected him belongs in the hands of survivors, investigators, law enforcement, Congress, and the public. It should never be withheld for months and then revealed as part of a commercial book release.
> Survivors have already endured decades of silence, delay, sealed records, broken promises, and institutional failure. They have watched powerful people avoid accountability while the truth has been selectively released, buried, or timed for someone else's benefit. That pattern must end. If journalists, publishers, government officials, law enforcement agencies, courts, political institutions, or any other individuals possess Epstein-related information that could help expose the network, identify those who enabled abuse, or bring accountability to survivors, it must be disclosed responsibly and without unnecessary delay.
> Survivors are not storylines. Their trauma is not content. Their pursuit of justice should never be timed around a publishing schedule, media rollout, or financial gain. Survivors have waited long enough. There can be no more selective transparency. No more delay. No more profit from survivors' pain while accountability remains out of reach.
> The truth must come out now.
> Lisa Phillips
> Lara Blume McGee
> Sharlene Rochard
> Audra Lynn Fasano
> Marina Lacerda
> Wendy Pesante
> Jena-Lisa Jones
> Jane Doe
> Jane Doe
> Jane Doe
Amen.
Again, predators couldn't do nearly as much damage. Last nearly as long in the shadows. Cultivate nearly as many victims. Without powerful protectors shielding them. And in this case also shielding Trump's inner-sanctum of political protectors.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ee1d00fd-acdd-4edc-a26d-b7a2279da64c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But to the ethically bereft gazing into their magic mirror to inquire who's the fairest in all the land, the "it's just one terrible man" horseshit is easy to sell. Why?
Because we love monster stories. They let the rest of us off the hook.
If Jeffrey Epstein _is the_ _whole_ story, then we're not talking about the billionaires who socialized with him. The universities that welcomed him. The institutions that knew--and still took his money. The corporate chieftains, law partners, and other elites who covered for him--including Haberman and Swan, who profited from burying parts of the story til their release fit nicely with their scheduled book-tour.
Then there are those who remained Epstein friends, clients, business partners, or investors. Even after Epstein was judged guilty in Florida almost exactly 18 years go, on state charges of _procuring a minor for prostitution_ and soliciting a prostitute.
Unlike these protectors, I won't allow the horrors to be buried.
I remind you of the role of one of the most powerful Republicans of the 21st Century in covering up a pedophile ring of Congress members and underage pages--and his eventual implication in the same crimes.
And even though it was difficult for me, I **name names from my high school, Horace Mann, who engaged in/covered up pedophilia** , including my onetime mentor. And share a rarely seen report by a first of its kind _Manhattan DA Sex Crimes Prosecution Bureau._
_**I won 't be a protector:**_**I remind you of** **the pedophilia and its protection by one of the most powerful Republicans.** Though uncomfortable, **I name names at** **Horace Mann --including my mentor.**

| Letter from the Chair
---
Momentum Building: Together, We Win!
As many of you know, Nebraska Republicans gathered in La Vista for our State Convention and left standing behind a full slate of nominees and one clear mission: Get Out the Vote. That energy hasn't faded. If anything, it's sharpened.
Much of that momentum traces back to a single moment at convention: when our federal and statewide candidates took the stage together, side by side, making clear this is one team running on one mission. That kind of visible togetherness doesn't happen by accident, and delegates noticed. It set the tone for everything since. Since convention, our Republican candidates have been on the move, talking to voters, building coalitions, and making the case for Nebraska values in every corner of the state. The theme that rang through the convention hall, "Together, We Win!", isn't a slogan we packed up and put away. It's the operating plan for the summer ahead.
This is the part of the cycle where the real work happens. Conventions generate energy. Summer is where that energy turns into doors knocked, calls made, and voters reached. Every county party, every precinct captain, every volunteer matters more right now than at almost any other point in the calendar.
Our nominees are ready to fight for Nebraska. Now it's on all of us to make sure every voter knows it.
Nebraska Republicans Won't Be Fooled
As the general election field comes into focus, one thing remains certain: Nebraska Republicans will continue to reject so-called "pseudo-Independents" and "Nonpartisans" who try to bypass our party's nomination process to sneak onto the general election ballot.
If a candidate cannot face Republican voters in a Primary, they are unlikely to earn their support in November. Why hide behind petition signatures instead of standing before county party members, defending your positions, and earning the trust of those who do the real work?
The easiest thing in politics is getting your name on a ballot. File some paperwork. Gather a handful of signatures. The hard part, the honorable part, is earning the respect of grassroots Republicans by showing up at county meetings, working the precincts, and proving yourself in the trenches long before your name ever appears anywhere.
We've seen this play before. A candidate skips the Primary, skips the scrutiny, skips the accountability, and then asks for votes in November as if none of that matters. It does matter. The process exists for a reason: it tests candidates, it earns trust, and it builds the kind of grassroots support that actually wins elections. Bypassing it isn't a shortcut to legitimacy. It's an admission that a candidate couldn't survive the real test.
True conservatives don't run from scrutiny. They embrace it.
Nebraska Republicans see through these tactics every time. We stand firmly behind our duly nominated candidates, in word and in deed. Real change comes through the Republican Party, not around it. And as petition deadlines and ballot announcements roll in over the coming weeks, we'll be watching closely and calling it out every time we see it.
Let's keep carrying the momentum from our State Convention through a strong summer of voter outreach. Together, we will win in 2026 and keep delivering results for Nebraska families. Forward together!

In Liberty and in Truth, Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

| State Senator Spotlight, Senator Rick Holdcroft - LD 36
Parents know what is best for their children - not the government. As a father and grandpa, I understand the importance of keeping parents involved in their children's lives. But out-of-touch politicians and government bureaucrats have attempted to put government at the center of children's lives.
When I was elected, I promised I would stand for faith, family, and freedom. That's why I'm fighting every day to protect common sense and keep parents in charge of raising their children. In the Legislature, I worked hand in hand with fellow Republican Senators to keep big tech companies from influencing and guiding children's lives without parental involvement.
Parents deserve transparency and accountability from schools, government agencies, and big tech companies. Moms and dads deserve to know what their children are being taught, what content they are being exposed to online, and who is influencing them. The government should support parents - not replace them.
Unfortunately, too many politicians believe bureaucrats know better than families. I strongly disagree. Strong families are the foundation of a strong Nebraska. When parents are empowered, children succeed, communities thrive, and our values are preserved for future generations.
That's why I have supported policies that defend parental rights, protect children online, and push back against government overreach. I will continue standing up for Nebraska values by defending faith, protecting freedom, and ensuring parents remain the primary decision-makers in their children's lives.
Nebraska families deserve leaders who trust parents, not government bureaucrats. I will always stand with parents. My campaign is driven by hardworking Nebraskans who value faith, family, and freedom. When I was elected, I promised I would stand for faith, family, and freedom. That's why I'm fighting every day to protect common sense and keep parents in charge of raising their children. In the Legislature, I worked hand in hand with fellow Republican Senators to keep big tech companies from influencing and guiding children's lives without parental involvement. Parents deserve transparency and accountability from schools, government agencies, and big tech companies. Moms and dads deserve to know what their children are being taught, what content they are being exposed to online, and who is influencing them. The government should support parents - not replace them. Unfortunately, too many politicians believe bureaucrats know better than families. I strongly disagree. Strong families are the foundation of a strong Nebraska. When parents are empowered, children succeed, communities thrive, and our values are preserved for future generations. That's why I have supported policies that defend parental rights, protect children online, and push back against government overreach. I will continue standing up for Nebraska values by defending faith, protecting freedom, and ensuring parents remain the primary decision-makers in their children's lives. Nebraska families deserve leaders who trust parents, not government bureaucrats. I will always stand with parents. My campaign is driven by hardworking Nebraskans who value faith, family, and freedom. Dear Friend, The last several weeks have been a defining stretch for the Freedom Caucus movement.Recent primaries brought real setbacks in some states, major victories in others, and a clear reminder that the political establishment now sees our members as a serious threat to its power. But elections are only part of the story. Across the country, State Freedom Caucuses are also delivering major policy wins, putting reforms before voters, and proving that organized conservatives can change what happens inside state capitols.
---
|
---
**GOP PRIMARIES - HALFTIME RECAP **This year’s primary elections have so far delivered both victories and setbacks for the Freedom Caucus movement. In Idaho and South Dakota, several of our members were defeated. We won’t sugarcoat it. Those losses hurt.In Idaho, liberal Republican Governor Brad Little and the special interests aligned behind establishment candidates not only against our members, but against conservative lawmakers across the state. When the votes were counted, five of our members had been defeated. In South Dakota, voters continued a recent trend of aggressively targeting incumbents. Two years ago, fourteen incumbents lost their seats in what many described as a political earthquake. This year, the electorate went even further, defeating sixteen incumbents, including several members of the **South Dakota Freedom Caucus**.But those results tell only part of the story. What we are witnessing across the country is not the decline of the Freedom Caucus movement. Quite the opposite.The Freedom Caucus model has become influential enough that the political establishment now views it as an existential threat to its power.That means our members are being targeted with more money, more opposition, and more coordinated attacks than ever before.And in many states, despite those attacks, the movement is growing. **Montana Freedom Caucus** members spent the past two years exposing the liberal Republicans who routinely teamed up with Democrats to block conservative reforms. Earlier this month, Freedom Caucus members and their recruited candidates defeated five of those legislators in Republican primaries and are positioned to significantly expand their ranks after November. In South Carolina, every incumbent Freedom Caucus member won re-election. Even more importantly, the Caucus is poised to add a few new members to its ranks. Considering the relentless attacks directed at the **South Carolina Freedom Caucus** since its formation in 2022, those victories represent a remarkable endorsement from conservative voters. Other states, including Oklahoma, Illinois, Georgia, West Virginia, and Pennsylvania, also made modest gains and are well positioned heading into the 2027 legislative sessions.The bottom line is simple: the Freedom Caucus movement is no longer an experiment.It is now a permanent force in state politics.And the establishment knows it.In fact, establishment Republicans in Wyoming recently spent money on billboards urging voters to “Stop the Freedom Caucus Agenda.” (see image below)Think about that for a moment.The irony is almost too perfect. A "Republican"-funded billboard telling Republican voters to stop Republicans from advancing conservative policies. The political establishment isn’t spending money attacking Freedom Caucus members because they’re ineffective. They’re attacking Freedom Caucus members because they understand exactly what is at stake.When lawmakers begin challenging the lobbyists, the bureaucracies, the special interests, and the comfortable arrangements that have dominated state capitols for decades, the Swamp fights back. Looking ahead, we still have important primary elections in Maryland, Minnesota, Missouri, Arizona, and Wyoming. The Establishment understands what is at stake and will continue targeting Freedom Caucus members wherever it can.But we know something they don’t. Conservative voters are increasingly recognizing the difference between Republicans who campaign as conservatives and Republicans who actually govern as conservatives.And that recognition is changing state politics across the country.
---
---
|
---
**MISSOURI** While primary elections have dominated recent headlines, it’s worth remembering why these races matter in the first place. The **Missouri Freedom Caucus** just completed one of the most successful legislative sessions of any Freedom Caucus in the country.This year, the **Missouri Freedom Caucus** helped lead the fight to reduce state spending, resulting in a budget that was approximately $4.1 billion smaller than the previous year’s budget. They also played the lead role in advancing Missouri’s new 7-1 congressional map, helping strengthen President Trump’s majority in Congress.And after years of effort, the **Missouri Freedom Caucus** successfully helped place Amendments 4 and 5 on the August ballot. Those measures address some of the most important issues facing Missouri voters, including protecting the initiative petition process from abuse and creating a pathway to eliminating Missouri’s income tax.These victories didn’t happen overnight.They are the result of years of organizing, educating voters, building coalitions, and refusing to back down when the political establishment said it couldn’t be done. That’s what the Freedom Caucus model looks like when it succeeds.Not just winning elections.Delivering results.
---
|
---
**ARIZONA** The Arizona Legislature successfully advanced the Arizona SAVE Act** \- sponsored by Arizona Freedom Caucus's State Rep. Alex Kolodin - **placing it on the November ballot.If approved by voters, the measure would:⚡️Require proof of citizenship⚡️Require voter ID⚡️Prohibit foreign money in elections⚡️Strengthen protections against fraudulent mail-in voting The significance here is that while the U.S Senate continues to stall out on the federal SAVE America Act, Arizona voters will have the opportunity to decide election integrity reforms directly.As the **Arizona Freedom Caucus** argued throughout the process, these are reforms that citizens have repeatedly demanded.Now the voters themselves will have the final say.
---
|
---
**RADIO CLIP OF THE WEEK** Our **_State Freedom Caucus Unfiltered_** radio show continues to air each week on NewsTalkSTL in St. Louis every Sunday at 8pm ET. If you’re not already listening, you can also subscribe to the podcast version using the links below.This week, South Carolina State Representative Thomas Beach, a founding member of the **South Carolina Freedom Caucus** , joined the program.In the clip below, Beach explains one of the oldest tricks in politics: giving a bill a title that sounds conservative, taxpayer-friendly, or reform-minded while hiding provisions in the fine print that accomplish the exact opposite.Most lawmakers vote based on talking points and press releases. Freedom Caucus members read the bills. That’s why the **South Carolina Freedom Caucus** has become so effective at exposing bad legislation before it becomes law.Have a listen:

clean_body: | | | | | Dear Friend, The last several weeks have been a defining stretch for the Freedom Caucus movement.Recent primaries brought real setbacks in some states, major victories in others, and a clear reminder that the political establishment now sees our members as a serious threat to its power. But elections are only part of the story. Across the country, State Freedom Caucuses are also delivering major policy wins, putting reforms before voters, and proving that organized conservatives can change what happens inside state capitols. | GOP PRIMARIES - HALFTIME RECAP This year’s primary elections have so far delivered both victories and setbacks for the Freedom Caucus movement. In Idaho and South Dakota, several of our members were defeated. We won’t sugarcoat it. Those losses hurt.In Idaho, liberal Republican Governor Brad Little and the special interests aligned behind establishment candidates not only against our members, but against conservative lawmakers across the state. When the votes were counted, five of our members had been defeated. In South Dakota, voters continued a recent trend of aggressively targeting incumbents. Two years ago, fourteen incumbents lost their seats in what many described as a political earthquake. This year, the electorate went even further, defeating sixteen incumbents, including several members of the South Dakota Freedom Caucus.But those results tell only part of the story. What we are witnessing across the country is not the decline of the Freedom Caucus movement. Quite the opposite.The Freedom Caucus model has become influential enough that the political establishment now views it as an existential threat to its power.That means our members are being targeted with more money, more opposition, and more coordinated attacks than ever before.And in many states, despite those attacks, the movement is growing. Montana Freedom Caucus members spent the past two years exposing the liberal Republicans who routinely teamed up with Democrats to block conservative reforms. Earlier this month, Freedom Caucus members and their recruited candidates defeated five of those legislators in Republican primaries and are positioned to significantly expand their ranks after November. In South Carolina, every incumbent Freedom Caucus member won re-election. Even more importantly, the Caucus is poised to add a few new members to its ranks. Considering the relentless attacks directed at the South Carolina Freedom Caucus since its formation in 2022, those victories represent a remarkable endorsement from conservative voters. Other states, including Oklahoma, Illinois, Georgia, West Virginia, and Pennsylvania, also made modest gains and are well positioned heading into the 2027 legislative sessions.The bottom line is simple: the Freedom Caucus movement is no longer an experiment.It is now a permanent force in state politics.And the establishment knows it.In fact, establishment Republicans in Wyoming recently spent money on billboards urging voters to “Stop the Freedom Caucus Agenda.” (see image below)Think about that for a moment.The irony is almost too perfect. A "Republican"-funded billboard telling Republican voters to stop Republicans from advancing conservative policies. The political establishment isn’t spending money attacking Freedom Caucus members because they’re ineffective. They’re attacking Freedom Caucus members because they understand exactly what is at stake.When lawmakers begin challenging the lobbyists, the bureaucracies, the special interests, and the comfortable arrangements that have dominated state capitols for decades, the Swamp fights back. Looking ahead, we still have important primary elections in Maryland, Minnesota, Missouri, Arizona, and Wyoming. The Establishment understands what is at stake and will continue targeting Freedom Caucus members wherever it can.But we know something they don’t. Conservative voters are increasingly recognizing the difference between Republicans who campaign as conservatives and Republicans who actually govern as conservatives.And that recognition is changing state politics across the country. | MISSOURI While primary elections have dominated recent headlines, it’s worth remembering why these races matter in the first place. The Missouri Freedom Caucus just completed one of the most successful legislative sessions of any Freedom Caucus in the country.This year, the Missouri Freedom Caucus helped lead the fight to reduce state spending, resulting in a budget that was approximately $4.1 billion smaller than the previous year’s budget. They also played the lead role in advancing Missouri’s new 7-1 congressional map, helping strengthen President Trump’s majority in Congress.And after years of effort, the Missouri Freedom Caucus successfully helped place Amendments 4 and 5 on the August ballot. Those measures address some of the most important issues facing Missouri voters, including protecting the initiative petition process from abuse and creating a pathway to eliminating Missouri’s income tax.These victories didn’t happen overnight.They are the result of years of organizing, educating voters, building coalitions, and refusing to back down when the political establishment said it couldn’t be done. That’s what the Freedom Caucus model looks like when it succeeds.Not just winning elections.Delivering results. | ARIZONA The Arizona Legislature successfully advanced the Arizona SAVE Act \- sponsored by Arizona Freedom Caucus's State Rep. Alex Kolodin - placing it on the November ballot.If approved by voters, the measure would:⚡️Require proof of citizenship⚡️Require voter ID⚡️Prohibit foreign money in elections⚡️Strengthen protections against fraudulent mail-in voting The significance here is that while the U.S Senate continues to stall out on the federal SAVE America Act, Arizona voters will have the opportunity to decide election integrity reforms directly.As the Arizona Freedom Caucus argued throughout the process, these are reforms that citizens have repeatedly demanded.Now the voters themselves will have the final say. | RADIO CLIP OF THE WEEK Our State Freedom Caucus Unfiltered radio show continues to air each week on NewsTalkSTL in St. Louis every Sunday at 8pm ET. name: Malcolm Kenyatta (via Democrats.org)
subject: What’s on my mind this Juneteenth
body:
A day of remembrance
---
Derek, it’s DNC Vice Chair Malcolm Kenyatta. This weekend, people across the nation will be celebrating and honoring Juneteenth. This day is a commemoration of when the last groups of enslaved people in Texas finally got word of their emancipation on June 19, 1865 — two and a half years after the Emancipation Proclamation was issued in 1863. Juneteenth is a celebration of Black resilience, community, and the enduring struggle for freedom. It is also a reminder that liberation must be fought for, continually defended, and expanded. Let me be honest: The Supreme Court’s decision in _Louisiana v. Callais_ has jeopardized some of the rights that Black and Brown Americans fought so hard to have acknowledged. Since this decision, we’ve seen states like Louisiana, Tennessee, Alabama, and Florida rush to redraw their maps to silence Black and Brown voices and effectively rig November’s elections in Republicans’ favor. In Mississippi, the Republican governor is urging the legislature to redraw its legislative, state supreme court, and congressional lines before the 2027 elections, when state legislative seats will be on the ballot. My friends, this is a moment for us to choose. A moment where young people are asking whether or not they’ll inherit a world where the color of their skin determines the trajectory of their lives. **A moment for us to stand up and fight for change, because injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere.** At this moment, when our hard-fought rights are under attack, your support is more important than ever. In this moment, we need to stand together and not give in to the cynicism of those who say we can’t win again. Let’s get to work. Thank you for your dedication to helping our country, Malcolm Malcolm Kenyatta
Vice Chair
Democratic National Committee

name: Han Jones
subject: Today, the movement continues
body:
https://va4reprofreedom.org/ [https://va4reprofreedom.org/]
Friend,
As we celebrate Juneteenth, we honor the resilience, strength, and collective action that helped secure freedom for generations of Black Americans.
Juneteenth reminds us that freedom i s more than a historical milestone.
Freedom is the ability to live, thrive, and make decisions about our bodies, our families, and our futures with dignity and support.
It has been 161 years since Juneteenth was born. Yet, Black families still face disparities and inequities at the hands of American systems — including health care:
Black women are three to four times more likely to die from pregnancy-related complications than white women . And 80% of these deaths are preventable.
At Virginians for Reproductive Freedom, we’re fighting for a future where every person has the right to reproductive health care, every family can thrive, and every mother is treated with dignity and respect.
And on November 3, we are rallying all Virginians to vote “YES” to enshrine reproductive freedom into Virginia’s Constitution .
LEARN MORE [https://va4reprofreedom.org/]
Today, help us celebrate Juneteenth by shining a light on the importance of improving Black maternal health.
And support our movement [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vaforrepro-em?refcode=061926] to empower families and build a better future today.
In gratitude,
Han Jones

name: Chris Pappas
subject: Juneteenth
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=7286%2E582294%2ER49M5x)
It’s Juneteenth.
Today we commemorate the official end of slavery in the United States — **a defining moment in our nation’s continuing journey toward justice and equality for everyone.**
Juneteenth is a day to reflect on the hard-won progress that generations of Black Americans have fought for and a moment to acknowledge the work that remains.
The promise of freedom delivered on June 19, 1865, was historic, but the struggle for equity and opportunity continues to this day. We must keep fighting for these ideals.
When I voted to recognize Juneteenth as a federal holiday in 2021, I did so knowing that symbolic progress must be matched with _real action._ This day reminds us of our shared responsibility to confront injustice, reject racism in all its forms, and build a future where everyone has a fair shot — regardless of their race, background, income, or zip code.
**Let us honor this day not just with remembrance but with purpose. Together we can build a more perfect union rooted in equality, dignity, inclusion, and freedom for all of us.**
– Chris

Today, we celebrate Juneteenth — a day that marks the end of slavery in the United States and honors the resilience, strength, and contributions of Black Americans throughout our nation's history.

Every generation has been called to continue the work of building a country that lives up to its promises of freedom, equality, and opportunity for all. As we reflect on this important day, we must also recognize that the fight for justice is ongoing.

We owe it to those who came before us — and those who will come after us — to keep working toward a future where every person is treated with dignity and respect.
