Donald Trump is building a $400 million ballroom at the White House.
**And many of the wealthy donors and corporations helping pay for it have been rewarded with tens of billions of dollars in federal contracts.**
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133625300/628521415/789508428?refcode=260619&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNTg2ZDkzZi1lNzZiLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Gn9v0dr6qwh6fb3DXRZLJSJDrNvmVm2UewDTbzjo8h0=)
While working families are worried about rising costs, health care, and housing, some of the largest corporations in America are writing checks for Trump's vanity project — and then receiving massive government business in return.
**This is corruption, plain and simple — and Congress has a responsibility to investigate it.**
I’ve spent my time in Congress fighting for a government that works for the people, not for powerful insiders who can buy access and influence.
That's why I've pushed for transparency. That's why I've demanded accountability from this administration.**And that's why I won't stop asking tough questions, no matter how much Republicans would prefer we look the other way.**
The American people deserve to know whether government contracts are being awarded based on merit or political favoritism. They deserve to know who's benefiting, who's profiting, and who's being left behind.

name: Kristen McDonald Rivet
subject: Juneteenth
body:
|
#
Friend, Today, we honor Juneteenth – the day in 1865 when the last enslaved Black Americans in Galveston, Texas were finally informed of their freedom – more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation was signed. Juneteenth marks a significant chapter in our nation's history and serves as a reminder of both how far America has come and the work each generation does to build a stronger future. **I hope you’re able to take a moment and reflect on the importance of this date – what it has meant for the history of our country, and what it means for us today.** For my part, I’ll be starting my day in Flint, then attending events across Mid-Michigan to celebrate Juneteenth, honor its history, and spend time with members of our community. Days like today remind us that America’s story is one of constant progress – driven by ordinary people who work to make their communities stronger, expand opportunity, and leave a better future for the next generation. Thank you, Kristen McDonald Rivet

If President Donald Trump does not force Israel to halt its escalating attacks on Lebanon, Iran told mediators it is prepared to suspend the agreement signed this week and launch retaliatory strikes against Israel, a senior Iranian official told Drop Site.
"Regarding Lebanon, we have warned both the mediators and the American side that if the regime fails to comply with the existing agreement, Iran will respond with substantial military measures without prior public notice," said the Iranian official, who is not authorized to speak publicly. "Should the United States intervene, conditions particularly those related to the Strait of Hormuz could rapidly revert to a wartime environment."
On Friday, reports emerged that a ceasefire agreement had been reached between Israel and Hezbollah, but an Israeli official said that even with a ceasefire, Israel would not withdraw its forces from Lebanon. Another Israeli official told Channel 12 that Israel retains the right to strike against perceived threats, a common Israeli claim used to systematically violate ceasefire agreements in Gaza and Lebanon.
Over the past week, Israel has continued to relentlessly attack Lebanon, and its forces remain deeply entrenched in the south. In a barrage of more than 20 airstrikes on Thursday night, Israel killed at least 47 people, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry. Since March, when Hezbollah entered the war alongside Iran, Israel has killed more than 3,900 people in Lebanon and displace over 1.2 million. Hezbollah has continued to ferociously retaliate against Israel's military campaign and has stunned Israel with its ability to inflict losses on its occupation forces. More than 30 Israeli troops have been confirmed killed in action since March 2.
On June 14, as Iran and the U.S. were finalizing the terms of the memorandum of understanding, Israel bombed the southern Beirut suburb of Dahiyeh. Iran came within hours of striking Israel in response, but officials said Tehran ultimately agreed to hold its fire after securing last minute concessions from Trump. Iran had previously called attacks on Beirut an escalation that would not go unanswered.

The continued war in Lebanon and Iran's pervasive mistrust of Trump have called into question the viability of a lasting deal. Technical talks that were scheduled to begin Friday in Switzerland were postponed, with Iranian officials citing the continued attacks in Lebanon. Some officials have also denounced the prospect of Iranian leaders being photographed meeting with Trump or other U.S. officials responsible for assassinating the country's Supreme Leader. U.S. officials have acknowledged the delay, but have not confirmed the reason. Late Thursday, the White House said Vice President JD Vance--who has been put forward as the public face of the U.S. negotiations--would not be traveling to Switzerland as previously announced, saying, "The logistics of these negotiations have never been simple or predictable." A senior Pakistani official claimed the meeting was canceled because of religious observances related to the Islamic month of Muharram, a period of mourning for Shia Muslims.
The cancellation of what was initially portrayed as a formal signing ceremony, potentially featuring Trump, indicates the fragile nature of the entire process. "We fully recognize that the implementation of this memorandum will be highly challenging due to President Trump's unpredictable and volatile approach," said the Iranian official, who is not authorized to publicly speak about internal deliberations. "It is entirely possible that the Iran file, like several of Trump's other political and economic initiatives, will be abandoned before reaching completion."
As Israeli officials continue to publicly denounce Trump and the agreement, Vance has pushed back ferociously, offering an unprecedented rebuke of Israel from an administration that has given it carte blanche to expand its wars across the region.
"Trump is the only head of state in the entire world who is sympathetic to the nation of Israel at this moment in time, and he happens to be the head of state of the world's superpower. If I was in the cabinet of the Israeli government, I might not be attacking the only powerful ally that I have anywhere left in the entire world," Vance [said](https://substack.com/redirect/26f092e6-c36f-4854-b436-16730cdb2e12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a press conference Thursday, adding that Israeli leaders should "wake up and smell the reality."
In remarks aimed at Israel, Vance [told](https://substack.com/redirect/52488c86-bc46-418c-b259-8f681daab37f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) The New York Times, "You're a country of 9 million people. You can't just kill your way out of solving every single national security problem that you have." At the opening of the G7 summit in France Monday, Trump repeatedly criticized Israel, saying, "Israel has been fighting Hezbollah for too long and too many people are being killed."
The White House has frequently pushed stories to friendly media outlets involving anonymous officials depicting Trump and Netanyahu in conflict only to turn around and endorse more aggressive Israeli attacks in both Gaza and Lebanon. The tenor of this criticism and the fact that it is being aired publicly by Trump and Vance directly is a new development.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing intense criticism inside Israel as he kicks off his campaign for re-election, with members of his own cabinet and opposition politicians alike denouncing the Iran deal and warning him against withdrawing from Lebanon. Some prominent political leaders have called for an expansion of the war.
Netanyahu has sought to strike a diplomatic tone with Trump, whom he has called "the greatest friend Israel has ever had in the White House," but has sought to portray himself as capable of separating U.S. and Israeli interests. He has argued that Trump's agreement with Iran does not bind Israel. "We will stay in the Lebanon security buffer zone for as long as necessary," Netanyahu said on June 15. "Many times we see eye to eye," Netanyahu said of the U.S.-Israeli relationship, "and there are also cases in which we see less eye to eye. I am responsible for Israel's security interests. I stand up for them." Defense Minister Israel Katz proclaimed Monday, "We oppose the withdrawal of the Israeli army from Lebanon, despite all current and future pressures."
Iranian negotiators fought to have a complete Israeli withdrawal included in the memorandum of understanding, while the U.S. pushed for vague language about ceasing hostilities. In the end, the text declared "the immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts, including in Lebanon" and "ensuring the territorial integrity and sovereignty of Lebanon." While Iran argues that this language means Israel must withdraw its occupation forces, top Iranian officials, including Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, have suggested the issue may not be resolved until a comprehensive deal is signed by the U.S. and Iran. "Without the withdrawal of Israeli forces from the territories they occupied during this war, the war has not fully come to an end," Araghchi said Tuesday.

## Dueling Narratives
In the days since the terms of the memorandum of understanding signed by the U.S. and Iran became public, debate has spread in both countries. Trump is facing criticism from some of his most die-hard supporters who hoped he would continue to escalate the war and empower Israel to broaden its attacks on Lebanon. In Iran, there is [ferocious debate](https://substack.com/redirect/254305ea-063a-4d96-9e93-56fff80be8ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) within the elite political echelon and while Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said he gave his consent for the country's political leadership to sign the MOU, he asserted in a statement Thursday that he personally opposed some of its terms.
As the narrative battles continue to play out in both countries, the senior Iranian official, who has direct knowledge of Tehran's decision-making process, provided Drop Site with an extensive account of how Iranian negotiators viewed the process that led to the deal and offered an assessment of the ultimate feasibility of the framework.
Throughout the two months following the signing of an initial ceasefire and the meetings in Islamabad between U.S. and Iranian officials, negotiators have engaged in indirect negotiations aimed at reaching an agreement to end the war. In public, Trump adopted the belligerent tone of a conqueror, claiming Iranians were "begging" him to make a deal and pledging that Tehran would surrender, U.S. troops would enter Iran to take custody of its stockpile of highly enriched uranium, and that Iran would receive no money as part of a deal with the U.S.
Despite Trump's public bravado, the reality was that it was the U.S. that repeatedly sought talks on ending the war. As Drop Site [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/ee800877-f45f-4e80-96ab-9ed355634f51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Trump's Special Envoy Steve Witkoff began sending messages to Iranian officials days after the war began on February 28. Iran took the position that it needed to re-establish a deterrent and would not allow a de-escalation until it believed it had done so.
Behind the scenes, once serious indirect talks began, Iran's negotiators held firm to a set of red lines, among them: the Israeli war against Lebanon must be brought to an end, Iran would not agree to export its enriched uranium, and Iran is entitled to billions of dollars of its frozen assets.
"The formation of this memorandum was the result of persistent requests and insistence from the American side and various mediators," said the Iranian official. "Nevertheless, from the outset we opposed both unlawful wars launched against our country, and we welcomed the prospect of peace after repeated requests for de-escalation."
In the end, Trump agreed to Iran's proposal to break the agreement into two main phases. The first would address an end to the war, including in Lebanon, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, the architecture of financial compensation to Iran and a re-affirmation that Iran would not seek to produce or acquire a nuclear weapon. The second phase would involve an initial 60-day window to negotiate a comprehensive agreement on the future of Iran's nuclear enrichment, the fate of its current stockpile and, crucially for Iran, terms that would lead to a lifting of all economic sanctions.
The senior Iranian official said the terms in the agreement governing the lifting of the U.S. military blockade in the Strait of Hormuz and endorsing Iranian management of the waterway, as well as the financial commitments--lifting of sanctions, unfreezing of money, and the establishment of a $300 billion reconstruction fund--included in the MOU "constitute an official record and a clear indication of the failure of President Trump's policy that led to the initiation of two wars against Iran."
Iranian negotiators emphasize that they do not trust Trump and frequently point out that twice in one year the U.S. claimed to be negotiating with Iran only to launch wars against it in the midst of a diplomatic process. At the same time, they argue, the geopolitical reality has been fundamentally altered since February. Iran's use of asymmetric warfare, particularly in asserting control over the Strait of Hormuz, alongside its ability to launch ballistic missile and drone attacks across the region--combined with its refusal to capitulate to two nuclear powers--serve as a warning to the U.S. about the stakes of resuming the war.
"We were fully aware of the economic consequences of this conflict for the region and the wider international community. The prospect of a major disruption in the Strait of Hormuz was among the most significant factors that ultimately contributed to the emergence of peace," the Iranian official said. "The immense costs imposed on all parties including extensive economic damage to countries across the region and the world were the price paid for President Trump's curiosity to experiment with the capabilities of the U.S. military."
Iranian officials say they intentionally negotiated for a deal structured through a reciprocal framework. If the U.S. does not abide by the terms, Iran has the ability to halt the process or respond militarily.
"This memorandum explicitly commits the United States to refraining from threats against Iran," said the Iranian official. "Should President Trump once again issue public threats against Iran, each such threat will be met with costs imposed on American interests in the region through new and evolving means. We would also implement corresponding pauses in the execution of certain commitments under the memorandum."
In his campaign to sell this deal as a victory, Trump has focused on the fact that Iran has formally agreed not to attempt to manufacture or procure a nuclear weapon. But this has been Iran's longstanding position, beginning with the 1970 signing of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, and was also stated explicitly in the 2015 Iran nuclear deal that Trump denounces daily. "Following two U.S.-Israeli wars against Iran, Washington once again succeeded only in obtaining Iran's reiterated commitment not to pursue nuclear weapons," the Iranian official said, saying "it was intentionally offered to President Trump as a symbolic concession, a cheap re-gift."
While Iran sought to exclude any commitments on its stockpile of enriched uranium, it eventually agreed to some terms. Trump consistently insisted that Iran could have no nuclear enrichment and that the U.S. would take custody of its roughly 1,000 pounds of 60% enriched uranium. Instead, the MOU says the U.S. and Iran agreed to "resolve the disposition of stockpiled, enriched material" with a "minimum methodology to be down-blending on site under the supervision" of the International Atomic Energy Agency. This approach precisely mirrors the terms Iran had proposed before the war began in February when it was negotiating with U.S. officials.
"The formal acceptance of all provisions by the United States constitutes both the consolidation and official declaration of the Trump administration's wartime policy," the Iranian official said, saying the terms of the "agreement were drafted in alignment with our national interests and the interests of the broader region."
Over the past several years, Iran has sought to deepen its ties with China, Russia, and other nations throughout the Eastern hemisphere. Since the launch of the 12-Day War in June 2025, Tehran has escalated efforts to expand its political, military and economic partnerships. Those efforts were kicked into high gear over the past four months. "This war will inevitably deepen our dependence on Eastern partners under circumstances imposed upon us. As a result, we will be compelled to pursue a far more rapid expansion of our security, economic, and political relations with China," the Iranian official said.
The February war called into question the viability of the rapprochement between Iran and several of its Arab allies in the Persian Gulf that preceded it, as the U.S. widely utilized military infrastructure to wage its war against Iran. Most Gulf nations portrayed Iran as the aggressor in the conflict, regularly denouncing its ballistic missile and drone strikes overwhelmingly aimed at U.S. military bases and facilities as unjustified attacks against their sovereignty. Now, Iranian officials say, many of these relationships are being repaired and discussions are ongoing about joint economic projects and elevated diplomatic ties.
If this agreement does lead to an end to the active military war--which remains a very open question--Iran will face its own domestic realities. The attacks by the U.S. and Israel have had an undeniable unifying effect on Iranian society, which has seen nightly mass gatherings in public squares. This rallying around the flag was also aided by Trump's threats to wipe out Iranian civilization and the attacks on civilians, including [the bombing](https://substack.com/redirect/728bdf03-0c5a-4707-bedd-3ebfe2b2e5db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the Minab girls school in the opening hours of the war. Israeli officials have made no secret of their intent to increase their covert actions in Iran, aimed at spurring an uprising. If the U.S. and Israeli bombing stops and Iran shifts from its role as fighting against the odds versus two nuclear powers, it will be left to face the economic and political issues confronting the country prior to the war. The extent to which the sense of unity on display since February will endure won't be clear for some time.
"Political and social divisions will require considerable time to heal," said the Iranian official. "The generational and institutional changes resulting from extensive assassinations and losses within Iran's political, security, and military leadership will undoubtedly create additional obstacles to the country's development."
There is no doubt Iran and the U.S. are at a historic crossroads in the era that began with the 1979 Islamic revolution. Because of the erratic nature of Trump and the way in which he integrates ego, personal ties, and efforts aimed at enriching his friends and family, Iran must approach any deal with the U.S. as subject to abandonment, violation, or cancellation. The 2015 nuclear deal took years to achieve, yet it was ripped up in an instant by Trump, kicking off a series of events that led to the first open wars launched by the U.S. against Iran since 1979.
"Our assessment is that, due to deficiencies in the expertise and technical preparedness of the American negotiating team, the specialized nuclear negotiations are unlikely to reach a mutually satisfactory conclusion within the proposed sixty-day timeframe," said the Iranian official. "Our military institutions will therefore remain on full alert. Furthermore, should a definitive assessment emerge indicating a renewed likelihood of U.S. military action against Iran, preemptive measures against an updated target bank would be considered."

A senior Pakistani official claimed the meeting was canceled because of religious observances related to the Islamic month of Muharram, a period of mourning for Shia Muslims. The cancellation of what was initially portrayed as a formal signing ceremony, potentially featuring Trump, indicates the fragile nature of the entire process. "We fully recognize that the implementation of this memorandum will be highly challenging due to President Trump's unpredictable and volatile approach," said the Iranian official, who is not authorized to publicly speak about internal deliberations. "It is entirely possible that the Iran file, like several of Trump's other political and economic initiatives, will be abandoned before reaching completion." As Israeli officials continue to publicly denounce Trump and the agreement, Vance has pushed back ferociously, offering an unprecedented rebuke of Israel from an administration that has given it carte blanche to expand its wars across the region. "Trump is the only head of state in the entire world who is sympathetic to the nation of Israel at this moment in time, and he happens to be the head of state of the world's superpower. If I was in the cabinet of the Israeli government, I might not be attacking the only powerful ally that I have anywhere left in the entire world," Vance in a press conference Thursday, adding that Israeli leaders should "wake up and smell the reality." In remarks aimed at Israel, Vance The New York Times, "You're a country of 9 million people. You can't just kill your way out of solving every single national security problem that you have." At the opening of the G7 summit in France Monday, Trump repeatedly criticized Israel, saying, "Israel has been fighting Hezbollah for too long and too many people are being killed." The White House has frequently pushed stories to friendly media outlets involving anonymous officials depicting Trump and Netanyahu in conflict only to turn around and endorse more aggressive Israeli attacks in both Gaza and Lebanon. The tenor of this criticism and the fact that it is being aired publicly by Trump and Vance directly is a new development. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing intense criticism inside Israel as he kicks off his campaign for re-election, with members of his own cabinet and opposition politicians alike denouncing the Iran deal and warning him against withdrawing from Lebanon. Some prominent political leaders have called for an expansion of the war. Netanyahu has sought to strike a diplomatic tone with Trump, whom he has called "the greatest friend Israel has ever had in the White House," but has sought to portray himself as capable of separating U.S. and Israeli interests. He has argued that Trump's agreement with Iran does not bind Israel. "We will stay in the Lebanon security buffer zone for as long as necessary," Netanyahu said on June 15. "Many times we see eye to eye," Netanyahu said of the U.S.-Israeli relationship, "and there are also cases in which we see less eye to eye. I am responsible for Israel's security interests. I stand up for them." Defense Minister Israel Katz proclaimed Monday, "We oppose the withdrawal of the Israeli army from Lebanon, despite all current and future pressures." Iranian negotiators fought to have a complete Israeli withdrawal included in the memorandum of understanding, while the U.S. pushed for vague language about ceasing hostilities. In the end, the text declared "the immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts, including in Lebanon" and "ensuring the territorial integrity and sovereignty of Lebanon." While Iran argues that this language means Israel must withdraw its occupation forces, top Iranian officials, including Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, have suggested the issue may not be resolved until a comprehensive deal is signed by the U.S. and Iran. "Without the withdrawal of Israeli forces from the territories they occupied during this war, the war has not fully come to an end," Araghchi said Tuesday. | | ---|---|--- President Donald Trump receives a tour of Chateau de Versailles from President of France Emmanuel Macron ahead of a dinner on June 17, 2026 in Versailles, France. During the dinner, Trump signed the memorandum of understanding with Iran. Photo by Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images. Dueling Narratives In the days since the terms of the memorandum of understanding signed by the U.S. and Iran became public, debate has spread in both countries. Trump is facing criticism from some of his most die-hard supporters who hoped he would continue to escalate the war and empower Israel to broaden its attacks on Lebanon. In Iran, there is within the elite political echelon and while Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said he gave his consent for the country's political leadership to sign the MOU, he asserted in a statement Thursday that he personally opposed some of its terms. As the narrative battles continue to play out in both countries, the senior Iranian official, who has direct knowledge of Tehran's decision-making process, provided Drop Site with an extensive account of how Iranian negotiators viewed the process that led to the deal and offered an assessment of the ultimate feasibility of the framework. Throughout the two months following the signing of an initial ceasefire and the meetings in Islamabad between U.S. and Iranian officials, negotiators have engaged in indirect negotiations aimed at reaching an agreement to end the war. In public, Trump adopted the belligerent tone of a conqueror, claiming Iranians were "begging" him to make a deal and pledging that Tehran would surrender, U.S. troops would enter Iran to take custody of its stockpile of highly enriched uranium, and that Iran would receive no money as part of a deal with the U.S. Despite Trump's public bravado, the reality was that it was the U.S. that repeatedly sought talks on ending the war. As Drop Site , Trump's Special Envoy Steve Witkoff began sending messages to Iranian officials days after the war began on February 28. Iran took the position that it needed to re-establish a deterrent and would not allow a de-escalation until it believed it had done so. Behind the scenes, once serious indirect talks began, Iran's negotiators held firm to a set of red lines, among them: the Israeli war against Lebanon must be brought to an end, Iran would not agree to export its enriched uranium, and Iran is entitled to billions of dollars of its frozen assets. "The formation of this memorandum was the result of persistent requests and insistence from the American side and various mediators," said the Iranian official. "Nevertheless, from the outset we opposed both unlawful wars launched against our country, and we welcomed the prospect of peace after repeated requests for de-escalation." In the end, Trump agreed to Iran's proposal to break the agreement into two main phases. The first would address an end to the war, including in Lebanon, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, the architecture of financial compensation to Iran and a re-affirmation that Iran would not seek to produce or acquire a nuclear weapon. The second phase would involve an initial 60-day window to negotiate a comprehensive agreement on the future of Iran's nuclear enrichment, the fate of its current stockpile and, crucially for Iran, terms that would lead to a lifting of all economic sanctions. The senior Iranian official said the terms in the agreement governing the lifting of the U.S. military blockade in the Strait of Hormuz and endorsing Iranian management of the waterway, as well as the financial commitments--lifting of sanctions, unfreezing of money, and the establishment of a $300 billion reconstruction fund--included in the MOU "constitute an official record and a clear indication of the failure of President Trump's policy that led to the initiation of two wars against Iran." Iranian negotiators emphasize that they do not trust Trump and frequently point out that twice in one year the U.S. claimed to be negotiating with Iran only to launch wars against it in the midst of a diplomatic process. At the same time, they argue, the geopolitical reality has been fundamentally altered since February. Iran's use of asymmetric warfare, particularly in asserting control over the Strait of Hormuz, alongside its ability to launch ballistic missile and drone attacks across the region--combined with its refusal to capitulate to two nuclear powers--serve as a warning to the U.S. about the stakes of resuming the war. "We were fully aware of the economic consequences of this conflict for the region and the wider international community. The prospect of a major disruption in the Strait of Hormuz was among the most significant factors that ultimately contributed to the emergence of peace," the Iranian official said. "The immense costs imposed on all parties including extensive economic damage to countries across the region and the world were the price paid for President Trump's curiosity to experiment with the capabilities of the U.S. military." Iranian officials say they intentionally negotiated for a deal structured through a reciprocal framework. If the U.S. does not abide by the terms, Iran has the ability to halt the process or respond militarily. "This memorandum explicitly commits the United States to refraining from threats against Iran," said the Iranian official. "Should President Trump once again issue public threats against Iran, each such threat will be met with costs imposed on American interests in the region through new and evolving means. We would also implement corresponding pauses in the execution of certain commitments under the memorandum." In his campaign to sell this deal as a victory, Trump has focused on the fact that Iran has formally agreed not to attempt to manufacture or procure a nuclear weapon. But this has been Iran's longstanding position, beginning with the 1970 signing of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, and was also stated explicitly in the 2015 Iran nuclear deal that Trump denounces daily. "Following two U.S.-Israeli wars against Iran, Washington once again succeeded only in obtaining Iran's reiterated commitment not to pursue nuclear weapons," the Iranian official said, saying "it was intentionally offered to President Trump as a symbolic concession, a cheap re-gift." While Iran sought to exclude any commitments on its stockpile of enriched uranium, it eventually agreed to some terms. Trump consistently insisted that Iran could have no nuclear enrichment and that the U.S. would take custody of its roughly 1,000 pounds of 60% enriched uranium. Instead, the MOU says the U.S. and Iran agreed to "resolve the disposition of stockpiled, enriched material" with a "minimum methodology to be down-blending on site under the supervision" of the International Atomic Energy Agency. This approach precisely mirrors the terms Iran had proposed before the war began in February when it was negotiating with U.S. officials. "The formal acceptance of all provisions by the United States constitutes both the consolidation and official declaration of the Trump administration's wartime policy," the Iranian official said, saying the terms of the "agreement were drafted in alignment with our national interests and the interests of the broader region." Over the past several years, Iran has sought to deepen its ties with China, Russia, and other nations throughout the Eastern hemisphere. Since the launch of the 12-Day War in June 2025, Tehran has escalated efforts to expand its political, military and economic partnerships. Those efforts were kicked into high gear over the past four months. "This war will inevitably deepen our dependence on Eastern partners under circumstances imposed upon us. As a result, we will be compelled to pursue a far more rapid expansion of our security, economic, and political relations with China," the Iranian official said. The February war called into question the viability of the rapprochement between Iran and several of its Arab allies in the Persian Gulf that preceded it, as the U.S. widely utilized military infrastructure to wage its war against Iran. Most Gulf nations portrayed Iran as the aggressor in the conflict, regularly denouncing its ballistic missile and drone strikes overwhelmingly aimed at U.S. military bases and facilities as unjustified attacks against their sovereignty. Now, Iranian officials say, many of these relationships are being repaired and discussions are ongoing about joint economic projects and elevated diplomatic ties. If this agreement does lead to an end to the active military war--which remains a very open question--Iran will face its own domestic realities. The attacks by the U.S. and Israel have had an undeniable unifying effect on Iranian society, which has seen nightly mass gatherings in public squares. This rallying around the flag was also aided by Trump's threats to wipe out Iranian civilization and the attacks on civilians, including of the Minab girls school in the opening hours of the war. Israeli officials have made no secret of their intent to increase their covert actions in Iran, aimed at spurring an uprising. If the U.S. and Israeli bombing stops and Iran shifts from its role as fighting against the odds versus two nuclear powers, it will be left to face the economic and political issues confronting the country prior to the war. The extent to which the sense of unity on display since February will endure won't be clear for some time. "Political and social divisions will require considerable time to heal," said the Iranian official. "The generational and institutional changes resulting from extensive assassinations and losses within Iran's political, security, and military leadership will undoubtedly create additional obstacles to the country's development." There is no doubt Iran and the U.S. are at a historic crossroads in the era that began with the 1979 Islamic revolution. Because of the erratic nature of Trump and the way in which he integrates ego, personal ties, and efforts aimed at enriching his friends and family, Iran must approach any deal with the U.S. as subject to abandonment, violation, or cancellation. The 2015 nuclear deal took years to achieve, yet it was ripped up in an instant by Trump, kicking off a series of events that led to the first open wars launched by the U.S. against Iran since 1979. "Our assessment is that, due to deficiencies in the expertise and technical preparedness of the American negotiating team, the specialized nuclear negotiations are unlikely to reach a mutually satisfactory conclusion within the proposed sixty-day timeframe," said the Iranian official. "Our military institutions will therefore remain on full alert. Furthermore, should a definitive assessment emerge indicating a renewed likelihood of U.S. military action against Iran, preemptive measures against an updated target bank would be considered." ---
| |
---|---
On June 19th, 1865, in Galveston, Texas, more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation, enslaved people finally learned they were free. Today, 161 years later, we must remind ourselves of the ongoing struggle for true equality and recommit to fighting racism in our government, our institutions, and society at large. Less than two months ago, the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act in _Louisiana v. Callais_ , marking the biggest rollback of Black voting and political power in 150 years. **The systematic disenfranchisement of communities of color across the South that Republicans will pursue will be felt by generations of Americans.** Building a more inclusive America has and always will require people to stand up, organize, and fight for what’s right, especially when those in power bully us, threaten us, and try to silence our voices. **Team DLCC is proud to stand with state legislators nationwide, Democratic candidates, and supporters like you to commemorate Juneteenth.** In solidarity, Team DLCC

The fight for freedom is never over |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133628305/628530227/1793776944?refcode=emm_ffa_20260619_Juneteenth_v1s2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmZmFiYTE3Yi1lOTZiLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6GjQd3g9Mt5GT5gWntGr5TeWxqfz3NZUmKqrwKSdx_E=&emci=feaba17b-e96b-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b6d6&emdi=ffaba17b-e96b-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b6d6&ceid=1037277)

| | One-hundred and sixty-one years ago today, enslaved Black Americans in Galveston, Texas finally gained their freedom — nearly two and a half years after the Emancipation Proclamation had been signed. That was the day in 1865 when Union troops arrived, and when freedom in theory became freedom in practice. Now we honor the anniversary as Juneteenth. **Today’s holiday reminds us that progress doesn’t happen in one instant, or with one stroke of a pen. And it is never guaranteed.** Just look at what happened with Reconstruction. In the years after the Civil War, as Black men were able to vote throughout the South, many won elected office, delivering representation for communities that had been locked out of American democracy. But white supremacist Southerners responded with Jim Crow. Tactics like poll taxes, literacy tests, and violent intimidation prevented Black Americans from voting and systematically dismantled Black political strength. Generations of organizing led to the Civil Rights movement and the Voting Rights Act, finally making it possible for Black Southerners to once again build power. We remember this rhythm of progress and repression. For over a decade now, the far-right Supreme Court has gutted pillar after pillar of the Voting Rights Act, opening the doors to racially discriminatory voter suppression — and enabling new voting maps that rip representation away from Black and brown Southerners. In fact, Governor Brian Kemp called the Georgia General Assembly into a special session starting this week, on the eve of Juneteenth, to draw maps that would silence Black and brown voters. Don’t let anyone tell you that date was a coincidence. **But in honor of all the freedom fighters who came before us, we’ve organized alongside partners to fight back at the grassroots level.** As the special map-rigging session was set to begin, a coalition of civil rights organizations, labor unions, faith leaders, and community advocates gathered to speak out against it. Nearly 500 Georgians packed the Capitol, applying grassroots pressure and producing results: State House and Senate leaders announced that they wanted to take new maps off the table for this session. It was a clear win, but the fight for freedom is never over. Kemp says he still wants to rig new district lines, so we’ll keep fighting back for fair maps with fair representation. **And we will continue fighting to ensure equal access to the ballot box and an equal voice for everyone in our democracy. The legacy of this generations-long work lives on with Fair Fight Action and activists like you.** Happy Juneteenth, The Fair Fight Action Team

subject: You’d think Donald Trump paid for these ads…
disclaimer_text: paid for by MAGA Inc
body:
#
We found out this week that another $800,000 in outside money is coming into this race to save our corporate-backed opponent, Diana DeGette.
**That brings the total outside spending against Melat to more than $1,000,000.**
Some of this dark money is coming from shell PACs that only just recently filed with the FEC in order to hide their funders from Denver voters.
It could be AIPAC, Big Pharma, or any other special interest desperate to keep the status quo working for them and against working people. They know Melat will not take their money, answer their calls, or protect their bottom lines in Congress, so they’re spending hundreds of thousands of dollars to stop her.
Another PAC, one that’s spending $400,000 against us, has deep ties to the party establishment. At a time when they should be putting every resource they have into taking back the House, the Senate, and holding Trump accountable, they are flying into Denver to save an incumbent who has taken this seat and its voters for granted.
**_And the ads they’re running are so xenophobic – saying Melat “doesn’t belong in Denver” – you’d think they were paid for by MAGA Inc. or ICE._**
**How is that fighting Donald Trump?!**
We do not have to outraise them dollar for dollar, but we do have to spend smarter, organize harder, and make sure Denver voters hear from us before they hear another lie from a dark money PAC.
**[Can you split a donation of $15, $26, or anything you can right now between our campaign and Justice Democrats to help fight back?](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260619-1-mk.lM4bDk&refcode=em20260619-37927&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=2&akid=37927%2E1203867%2ESptr8p)**
**[Contribute $10](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260619-1-mk.lM4bDk&refcode=em20260619-37927&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=21&akid=37927%2E1203867%2ESptr8p)**
With your help, we will not let them buy this election.
Thank you,
Kiros for Congress

body:
We're celebrating Juneteenth, but the fight for equality is far from over.
These emails are the best way for our campaign to stay in touch with supporters like you. If you'd prefer to unsubscribe, [click here](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/7010?refcode=LOC_EM_NOFR_2026.06.19_Junetenth_B2_F1_S1_C1_actives-exp_N-T0&t=1&akid=6372%2E196590%2EgBdCia).
---
[](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/7008?refcode=LOC_EM_NOFR_2026.06.19_Junetenth_B2_F1_S1_C1_actives-exp_N-T0&t=2&akid=6372%2E196590%2EgBdCia)
| Folks, today is Juneteenth, the day Major General Gordon Granger arrived in Galveston, Texas, and announced that “all slaves are free” and “an absolute equality of personal rights” for Black Americans.

I’m feeling mixed emotions today. Part of me is filled with gratitude for the Black leaders who have fought tirelessly for equal rights throughout our history.

Another part of me is frustrated. Because more than 160 years later, the fight for equality is far from over. Black voting rights and representation are still under attack.

Trump’s Supreme Court greenlit racial gerrymandering, Republicans are attempting to erase Black history from schools and museums, and efforts to dismantle voting rights that civil rights leaders fought so hard to secure. Some Republicans, like Tom Tiffany, even voted against the creation of Juneteenth.

Days like today remind us where we’ve been, how much we’ve overcome, and how critical the fight ahead is. The fight for democracy, where all voices are heard, is ongoing. It’s happening everywhere, from Alabama to our own backyard in Wisconsin.

I refuse to stay silent while rights are threatened and communities are left behind. That’s why I’m running to be the next Governor of Wisconsin. I will keep fighting for a Wisconsin where everyone has equal representation and equality.

Happy Juneteenth.

Mandela Barnes

freedom is not just a moment in time

| Peter,

Earlier this week, I had the privilege of joining the Opening Night Celebration of the Annual Scotland Juneteenth Heritage Festival as well as the Kensington Juneteenth Festival and the Annual Scotland Juneteenth Interfaith Service. Feeling the energy of a community coming together to honor its history was a powerful reminder of what Juneteenth is all about: celebrating freedom, preserving our shared story, and recommitting ourselves to the work that remains.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133629272/628533488/-1721553747?refcode=BLU_EM_AFMC_2026-06-19_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiYjU0YmIzYy1lYjZiLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cthT50GEgcn5KR5gMUbVVzf7_JB_LrOW2hth3NKVuvE=)
Today and tomorrow, we will continue to honor and celebrate Juneteenth with the Annual Scotland Juneteenth Festival, the Pint Israel Baseball Classic and the County’s Annual Juneteenth Celebration at BlackRock. Juneteenth marks the end of slavery in the United States, not on paper but in practice, and honors the resilience, achievements, and contributions of Black Americans throughout our nation's history.

Juneteenth reminds us that freedom is not just a moment in time. It is a re-commitment that each generation is called to better understand, safeguard, and build upon for future generations.

As we reflect on this day, I am thinking about the people in our community and country whose courage, sacrifice, and determination helped move our country closer to its ideals. Their stories continue to inspire us to learn from our history, strengthen our communities, and build a future rooted in dignity, opportunity, and justice for all.

Today is also a day of celebration. Across Montgomery County and around the country, families, friends, neighbors, and organizations are gathering to honor culture, heritage, and the enduring spirit of those who never gave up hope for a better tomorrow.

I hope you'll join me in taking a moment to reflect on the meaning of this day, the history it represents, and the responsibility we all share to keep telling that full history and building stronger, more inclusive communities for future generations.

Happy Juneteenth, [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133629273/628533489/-1721553747?refcode=BLU_EM_AFMC_2026-06-19_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiYjU0YmIzYy1lYjZiLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cthT50GEgcn5KR5gMUbVVzf7_JB_LrOW2hth3NKVuvE=)

I enjoyed an amazing ice cream sundae bar and a great conversation about health care, Social Security, and more with my neighbors in Lebanon County last weekend.
**But what really makes people want to scream right now (besides ice cream!) is money in politics.**
I hear about it all the time on the campaign trail. People are fed up with the idea that politics is a coin machine, where you put money in and out comes something for you that other people don't get.
We're watching Dan Meuser double his net worth and have a better stock portfolio performance than Warren Buffett and Bill Gates. We're seeing him cut our health care to give billionaires a tax break. We're watching him host $3,500 minimum fundraisers for Mar-a-Lago mega-donors but refuse to ever hold a town hall.
We can look at corruption in politics and say, I want nothing to do with it. Or we can look at corruption in politics and fight to change it. I'm choosing to fight. I hope you'll join me.

The blood spilled on the Edmund Pettus Bridge, the courage of every marcher who made the Voting Rights Act possible—we cannot let it be undone quietly, without a fight.
| | | | | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001IhoHzlsrn-7-grnKBndT6KKvv0xT908fEhBqbvv_XtVePQ0yFI6svj-hd5IHt4t6-yMJRE3bBh0vhCF4XlNIInnmYMmiCw6Hew0aBci14TBTNnkZtdAujwKDemEP4i44Z7dKGnKn7QNM00hNzwbjte--gOig9Jh-S7kQQf_qZW1zsPp-fcWss_sgOa0hPMKEzPYCHAVB_sS4dRxjAD-bi3qsMV4Tq-wl&c=GsjxnY6f8cn4XiGKOoEAjl2cRVoaVTnEyVLqQu8FRAjHUx0bpmalZA==&ch=SEQ0xlqA_jUHLPVblwve8DeFkmtgcuMTA32x0vCSkgW4BOeQFU6I6Q==)
---
| Peter,
Today is Juneteenth.
Today we mark the day the last enslaved Americans learned they were free. Today we celebrate 161 years of Black resilience, Black power, and Black progress.
Freedom is not free. It never has been.
This year, the Supreme Court struck down the protections that made Black political power possible. Within weeks, Louisiana, Tennessee, and Alabama redrew their maps--cracking Black communities apart, breaking up Black-majority districts, stripping us of our voice in Congress.
---
| | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001IhoHzlsrn-7-grnKBndT6KKvv0xT908fEhBqbvv_XtVePQ0yFI6svj-hd5IHt4t6-yMJRE3bBh0vhCF4XlNIInnmYMmiCw6Hew0aBci14TBTNnkZtdAujwKDemEP4i44Z7dKGnKn7QNM00hNzwbjte--gOig9Jh-S7kQQf_qZW1zsPp-fcWss_sgOa0hPMKEzPYCHAVB_sSneeL2SXASWS1C7eBBDkWV&c=GsjxnY6f8cn4XiGKOoEAjl2cRVoaVTnEyVLqQu8FRAjHUx0bpmalZA==&ch=SEQ0xlqA_jUHLPVblwve8DeFkmtgcuMTA32x0vCSkgW4BOeQFU6I6Q==)
---
Our colleague Cleo Fields returned to Congress after 30 years, only to have his district wiped out again. Louisiana goes from two Black-majority districts to one, in a state where one in three residents is Black.
Jim Clyburn said it plainly: "This Supreme Court is resegregating this country."
The blood spilled on the Edmund Pettus Bridge, the courage of every marcher who made the Voting Rights Act possible--we cannot let it be undone quietly, without a fight.
[In honor of Juneteenth, will you chip in $19 to help the Louisiana Democrats defend Black representation in Congress?](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001IhoHzlsrn-7-grnKBndT6KKvv0xT908fEhBqbvv_XtVePQ0yFI6svj-hd5IHt4t6xs0VcngMeLpkDGfP22OABVD4v5P-UH8AQQtSXqfoarg6YP3a7THVSd9Ee34CUlWXMkqHAs_6zeH8nxCBw_GF7XijoXgjIebGcVrR1yevy1AOC4q70ZTEow8x01Z5DIqSmlvSzg5iEOLVAs5YYH6l1QkYcY4TYiSg9NmczYbUmek=&c=GsjxnY6f8cn4XiGKOoEAjl2cRVoaVTnEyVLqQu8FRAjHUx0bpmalZA==&ch=SEQ0xlqA_jUHLPVblwve8DeFkmtgcuMTA32x0vCSkgW4BOeQFU6I6Q==)

# [#]
Peter,

On this day in 1865, the news of emancipation reached Galveston, Texas, and the last enslaved people in the Confederacy were freed. Juneteenth marks a pivotal moment in American history. It is both a celebration of freedom and a reminder of the progress we have made.

Today, we honor the courage of those who waited, fought, and resisted. But as we remember this historic moment, we must also confront the inequity and racism still present in our nation today.

The reality is we are still in the fight against systemic inequities that remain against Black Americans, and we must recommit ourselves to the pursuit of justice for all. That means protecting voting rights and fighting back against policies that continue to hold people back.

Take some time today to learn, reflect, and celebrate our progress — and our ongoing work to secure equality for all.

Thank you,
Seth Magaziner

name: Aaron Ford
subject: Me, my kid brother, and a stale candy bar
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY SHAPIRO FOR PENNSYLVANIA
body:
No working parent should struggle to put food on the table for their kids. I should know. I’ve been that hungry kid, Derek. Growing up in a working-class family, I watched my mom and dad take on multiple jobs, and still struggle to put food on the table at the end of the day. **A few times, all my brother and I had for dinner was a stale candy bar. ** [****](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133632494/628539441/417780647?refcode=email_061926_aaronfordsplit&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyYzJiM2EzNy1lZTZiLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=7X2Oj2fVJzOWjy7e9_DI5M-DmhVV_uLIomH_r3TaOec=)_My parents doing everything they could was somehow not enough._ A lot has changed since then. I’ve earned multiple degrees and raised four boys with my wife, Berna. Today, I proudly serve Nevadans as our Attorney General. But no matter how far I’ve come or how far I’ll go, he stays with me: a kid looking for dinner on empty shelves and finding nothing but stale candy. And my story isn’t unique. Right now, it’s repeating itself across millions of Nevada homes. Parents heading to work before the sun rises. Extra hours, tightened belts, no end in sight – and it’s still not enough to get by in a broken economy. [**That’s why I’m running for Governor and urgently asking for your support. Can you split a contribution between Josh Shapiro and me today?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133632496/628539443/417780647?refcode=email_061926_aaronfordsplit&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyYzJiM2EzNy1lZTZiLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=7X2Oj2fVJzOWjy7e9_DI5M-DmhVV_uLIomH_r3TaOec=) _I’m running for Governor_ because the lifelines that got my family through the hardest times – Medicaid to stay healthy, food stamps to stay fed, public education as a path out of a rough neighborhood – are all under attack. Republicans are attacking the public programs that gave a kid like me a chance. Without them, I wouldn’t have made it this far. Neither will millions of Nevada families if we let them be gutted by the GOP. _I’m running for Governor_ because it’s getting worse. Gas prices are over $5 a gallon and rising across Nevada. From housing to health care to utilities, costs are unbearably high, and they’re crushing working families who are already stretched to the breaking point. _I’m running for Governor_ because the people in charge _don’t care_. Donald Trump and his MAGA sidekick, Republican Governor Joe Lombardo, aren’t going to fix this crisis. They’re not even trying. For anything to change, we must unseat Lombardo and elect a governor who takes this crisis seriously. I will – because I’ve lived it. [**If you can spare a few dollars, please split a donation between my campaign and Josh Shapiro to end the failed Lombardo-Trump economy and lower costs for every working family in Nevada. I don’t ask this lightly, but there is so much at stake.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133632498/628539445/417780647?refcode=email_061926_aaronfordsplit&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyYzJiM2EzNy1lZTZiLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=7X2Oj2fVJzOWjy7e9_DI5M-DmhVV_uLIomH_r3TaOec=) _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | | [Donate $5 →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133632500/628539447/417780647?refcode=email_061926_aaronfordsplit&amount=5&amounts=5,15,25,50,100&express_lane=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyYzJiM2EzNy1lZTZiLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=7X2Oj2fVJzOWjy7e9_DI5M-DmhVV_uLIomH_r3TaOec=)

June 19, 2026
Back when pterodactyls were a common sight in the overhead sky, I was a medical student. The tuition was $5,500 a year and three friends and I rented a four-bedroom house for $200 a month, $50 each. Beer was 75 cents. And served in a frosted mug.

Today [medical school tuition](https://substack.com/redirect/3322f860-eac4-4fbe-8baa-99fc6389bfc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at the University of Connecticut is over $50,000 and over $80,000 for non-residents. [Yale Medical Schoo](https://substack.com/redirect/fafe52df-689c-4d60-9e21-3a64efabe123?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)l is over $70,000. And studio apartments in a safe area of New Haven start at [$1,600 a month](https://substack.com/redirect/9e1cf69c-bf2c-4e19-8706-e0d6de35d9b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). No wonder socialism is popular with the young generation! I'd be a socialist too if I was being ripped off like this at age 25.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3543e01f-a221-493d-a9cc-e51ffabca13c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Graduates who may still be paying off student loans when they are on Social Security
The main reason tuitions have skyrocketed is because of easy access to unlimited student loans. President Trump wisely perceived this and [capped student loans](https://substack.com/redirect/5787c1fd-4273-4fe9-8e36-cb29294cfbf1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Those for professional graduate schools such law and medicine are capped at a total $200,000, $50,000 annually, and graduate schools such PhD programs are capped at a total of $100,000, $25,000 annually.
Baby Boomers have learned that easy credit is the best way to sucker the younger generations into overpaying for housing and education. They don't call us the "Me Generation" for nothing.
Now the Baby Boomer university professors, who are overwhelmingly liberal Democrats, are howling with indignation.

With caps on student loans, we have to lower our tuition! How dare these MAGA imbeciles cut into our fat salaries, pensions and Cadillac health insurance! How dare they cut into our green fees and Viking cruise plans!
This is why Attorney General Tong and a coalition of mostly Blue State Attorney Generals have [sued](https://substack.com/redirect/ac61976b-639b-453c-9118-3b76218e2958?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Department of Education to overturn these limits. According to Mr. Tong:

"The Trump/McMahon plan to magically drive down education costs by barring student loans defies Congress, defies the law, defies reality, and will do real damage to Connecticut students and workers. We are suing to restore common sense and to force Trump and McMahon to follow the law."
But these limits were not placed on student loans by a Donald Trump fiat. These limits were enacted by Congress. Contrary to Tong's statement, limits on student loans are the law. But Tong and other liberal attorney generals know how to manipulate our democratic process. Some liberal judge could ignore the law - as power hungry liberal judges enjoy doing - and rule in Tong's favor.

I recently had lunch with a young man who was finishing his training to be a physical therapist. His wife was almost done with her speech therapy degree. Their cumulative student debt was $400,000! Assuming that they are going to pay this load off over 20 years at 6%, this young couple has to come up with $2850 a month.
How are they going to buy a house? Will any bank give them a housing loan? How are they going to have children? They are nothing more than indentured servants to Tong's greedy liberal Baby Boomer constituency.
Retiring UConn medical doctors are raking in comfortable [six-figure pensions](https://substack.com/redirect/e3bfe92e-64c8-437a-9e0f-c40cc586a982?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with one doctor scoring over $335,000 a year. And these pensions increase annually based on inflation and are accompanied by Cadillac health insurance plans.
Lectures at professional schools could easily be placed on videotapes. Examinations are already done with computers. There is no reason to gouge our young aspiring professionals with lecturers raking in high salaries and fat pensions.
Furthermore, Democrats such as Congressman Larson are now beating the drums to shore up social security by taxing billionaires. Of course this is nonsense. Even a huge tax on billionaires would not come close to maintaining the Social Security benefits that have been promised.

What Larson really wants to do is increase the FICA (Federal Insurance Contributions Act) tax of 7.5% - of which another 7.5% must be matched by the employer - on our young people.

Is this fair? We Baby Boomers have had a great life. Those of us who saved can have frequent vacations. Those who did not are not going to starve. Why should the younger generation pay outrageous taxes, housing prices and tuitions to support our extravagent lifestyles?
This nonsense needs to stop. And the first step is capping student loans.

name: Squad Victory Fund
subject: Celebrating Juneteenth
body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20260619-2384-foote&t=1001&akid=2384%2E342411%2E3u7idQ ]Squad Victory Fund

Peter,

161 years ago to the day, Union soldiers arrived in Texas and announced
the news of emancipation — nearly two and a half years after the
Emancipation Proclamation was issued. Today, we celebrate this day as
Juneteenth.

And while we take this day to celebrate together, we want to reaffirm our
commitment to the ongoing fight for Black justice.

Today, far too many systems continue to perpetuate the wounds of racism
entrenched in our institutions. And under the Trump administration, this
pattern has only worsened.

We’ve seen attacks on programs that help families access health care and
put food on the table. We’ve seen the rollback of DEI programs in
workplaces and schools. And, less than two months ago, we watched the
Supreme Court gut the Voting Rights Act — opening the door for states to
enact discriminatory voting maps and diluting Black political power.

These setbacks are real,
Peter — but so is the legacy of
those who refuse to accept them.

Every step forward in our country’s history happened because ordinary
people showed up, organized, and demanded necessary change. The freedoms
we celebrate on Juneteenth were not simply granted — they were won through
generations of Black leadership, courage, and resilience in the face of
oppression.

That’s the spirit we celebrate today.

Today calls us to honor how far we’ve come while staying focused on how
far we still need to go in the fight for racial justice. We don’t have
another 161 years to wait. And we don’t have generations to spare before
every family can thrive, every vote can count, and every community can
share in the promise of democracy.

The work continues now. As a Squad, we’re proud to be part of the movement
committed to fighting for racial justice in Washington and for our
communities nationwide.

Happy Juneteenth. Black lives matter. Black joy matters. Black futures
matter.

In solidarity,

The Squad Victory Fund

body:
I’m proud that we’ve shown what happens in Michigan when Democrats lead |
#
---
On Juneteenth, we commemorate the day when the last enslaved Americans in Galveston, Texas learned they were free, more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation was issued. Juneteenth is an opportunity to celebrate Black history, culture, and achievement while reflecting on the work it has taken to move our country forward. The promise of freedom and opportunity has always required people to speak up, show up, and insist that America live up to its values — _even when progress feels too slow or out of reach._ That's a lesson worth remembering today. Here in Michigan, I’m proud that we've worked to back up our values with action. We’ve protected voting rights, banned hair discrimination, invested in working families, and created more opportunity for people across our state. I firmly believe that everyone deserves to feel seen, valued, and empowered to reach their full potential, and I’m proud of the work we’ve done in Michigan to forward this progress. Today, let's honor the resilience and contributions of Black Americans who have helped shape our nation for generations. And let's recommit ourselves to continuing the work of building stronger communities and a brighter future for all. Thank you for being part of this work. name: LeftNet
subject: June 19, 1865
body:
161 years ago today.
#
On June 19th 1865, Union soldiers informed the last enslaved people in Galveston, Texas, of their freedom — some two and a half years after President Lincoln’s Emancipation Proclamation.
And though it’s only been a federal holiday since 2021, Juneteenth is a significant day celebrating the liberation and freedom of Black Americans in what has become known as our country’s second Independence Day.
But as we celebrate today, we must remember and recognize how the Black community continues to make a way out of no way, overcoming trials and structural hurdles that have remained in place to defer true justice and equality.
The importance of celebrating Juneteenth, then, like now, recognizes the ongoing fight for equality, accountability, and, moreover, to laud Black resilience and achievements while continuing to aid in the preservation of the narratives and moments in time that have advanced racial justice since 1865.
We hope you’re able to join us today to celebrate the progress that we’ve made and reflect on the challenges ahead.
Happy Juneteenth.
— LeftNet

clean_body: 161 years ago today. On June 19th 1865, Union soldiers informed the last enslaved people in Galveston, Texas, of their freedom — some two and a half years after President Lincoln’s Emancipation Proclamation. And though it’s only been a federal holiday since 2021, Juneteenth is a significant day celebrating the liberation and freedom of Black Americans in what has become known as our country’s second Independence Day. But as we celebrate today, we must remember and recognize how the Black community continues to make a way out of no way, overcoming trials and structural hurdles that have remained in place to defer true justice and equality. The importance of celebrating Juneteenth, then, like now, recognizes the ongoing fight for equality, accountability, and, moreover, to laud Black resilience and achievements while continuing to aid in the preservation of the narratives and moments in time that have advanced racial justice since 1865. We hope you’re able to join us today to celebrate the progress that we’ve made and reflect on the challenges ahead. Happy Juneteenth. — LeftNet LeftNet is an online political network fighting for progressive causes and candidates focused on social, racial, economic, and environmental justice.

Team: Mail-in ballots are under attack. Again.
The Supreme Court agreed to hear arguments in RNC v. Wetzel, a lawsuit challenging Mississippi’s law allowing a five-day grace period for late-arriving ballots mailed by Election Day. In simpler terms, it's a case about whether your vote will count if you mail it on or before Election Day, but your ballot arrives after Election Day.
It's clear why a political party -- in this case, the Republican National Committee (RNC) -- is claiming that states must reject ballots that arrive after Election Day. Doing so would potentially disenfranchise a large number of voters, restricting the number of participants in an election. And the data is clear, over the last several election cycles, Republicans have been outnumbered in the use of mail-in ballots.
The RNC is making a blunt decision that their ability to win elections matters more than your vote. It's a cynical attempt to stay in power by suppressing ballots that are delivered late by the postal service. It's the kind of partisan work that shows they'd rather believe in their own power and control than the principles of democracy, of a country where all our votes should count, regardless of party.

This shouldn't be a partisan question. No political party -- Democrat, Republican, Green, Working Families, Libertarian, Reform, Conservative -- should be against voting. No party in our democracy should want to restrict the fundamental right of our fellow citizens to make their voice heard through voting.
But now we're facing a case where the Supreme Court’s decision could strike down or uphold laws in 16 states (and Washington D.C.) allowing late-arriving ballots postmarked on or before Election Day to be counted if they arrive within a set grace period.

Data from the 2024 Massachusetts elections shows that their three-day grace period for ballots to arrive after Election Day resulted in a 60% drop in rejected ballots as compared to no grace period. Today, we celebrate Juneteenth — a day that honors generations of Black Americans who fought to make our country live up to its promise of freedom and equality.

Juneteenth is not just Black history. It is American history.

In Trump’s America, he’s throwing the history of Black Americans’ struggles in the shredder to make room for yet another tribute to himself. Case in point? National parks are now free on Trump's birthday, but not on Juneteenth or Martin Luther King Jr. Day.

To me, honoring Juneteenth means more than celebrating a date on the calendar. It means building a country where freedom and opportunity are accessible to everyone.

It means advancing climate policies that protect communities too often left behind, reforming our housing system so families can afford a place to live, creating quality healthcare, good-paying jobs, and economic opportunities that are truly available to all.

That's the future I'm fighting for in Congress. And as MAGA extremists work to erase history and turn us against one another, I'll keep working toward a more just, inclusive, and equitable America — one that lives up to the promise Juneteenth represents.

Together,

Yassamin Ansari

name: David Hogg
subject: Juneteenth
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
#
**Today, we mark Juneteenth, Peter.**
It’s a day to honor liberation, to remember the Black Americans who fought for their own freedom, and to celebrate the profound joy of a community that survived the unimaginable.
The official end of slavery in 1865 is worth celebrating. But we can’t pretend that racism, discrimination, and disenfranchisement only happened in history books.
Right now, we are witnessing a sustained assault on the rights of Black Americans. Look at what just happened to the Voting Rights Act. For 60 years, Section 2 was one of our last lines of defense against politicians trying to take away Black representation. Then, six conservative justices decided that defense didn't matter anymore.
Because of that decision, states are now drawing maps explicitly designed to split up communities, erase majority-Black districts, and silence voters. And this isn’t just about Congress. It’s going to impact state legislatures, city councils, and school boards across the country — the exact places where Black communities have fought the hardest to see themselves represented.
One piece of our mission at Leaders We Deserve is removing the barriers that have tried to keep young Black leaders from holding power. Our election system has always favored those who are older, wealthy, and white. But real change happens when the people with diverse lived experience are the ones writing the laws.
**That’s why Leaders We Deserve candidates like Justin J. Pearson, Christian Menefee, Donavan McKinney, Dinah Escarment, and Tyler Smith aren't backing down.** They didn’t wait for permission to show up for their communities, and they go even harder when the system is stacked against them.
Juneteenth is a reminder of where we’ve been, how far we’ve come, and how hard we still need to fight for equality, justice, and representation for everyone.
I deeply appreciate your support as we continue doing this important work.
In solidarity,
David Hogg

Today, we celebrate Juneteenth, the day enslaved people in Texas learned they were finally free, two years after the Emancipation Proclamation was signed.
Juneteenth is a celebration of how far we've come, a reaffirmation that Black history is American history, no matter how some people try to erase it, and a reminder of the work that needs to be done. The fight for equal rights, enfranchisement, and fair representation did not end in 1865. It continues today. I’m grateful to the brave men and women who, throughout our history, fought for freedom for all.

They call us “radicals.”
They call us “extremists.”
They call us “deplorables.”
The media mocks us. The Hollywood elites look down on us. The D.C. swamp tries to break us every single day.

Dark money is moving fast. We have to move faster. So please, split $10 between my campaign and Blue Amp Action to help me win in 2026:**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/10889?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.06.19_Dunn-Lost_B2_F1_S4_C4_90AC-365DON_RS-T0&t=5&akid=2512%2E259176%2EcMseWw) | [JOIN THE FIGHT >>](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/10889?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.06.19_Dunn-Lost_B2_F1_S4_C4_90AC-365DON_RS-T0&t=6&akid=2512%2E259176%2EcMseWw)
---
In 2024, I ran for Congress in Maryland. I fought as hard as I knew how. I knocked on doors, made calls, and connected with voters.
The voters who heard my message? They were with me.
_The problem was getting heard at all._
Dark money donors spent MILLIONS of dollars to drown me out, and it worked. I watched it happen in real time — ads I couldn't match, mailers I couldn't answer, and a wall of money between me and the voters I was trying to reach.
When you have that kind of money, you don't have to win the argument. You just have to make sure the other side can't be heard.
I could've walked away. God knows it would've been easier.
But I filed to run again.
**I stood inside the United States Capitol on January 6th and watched Donald Trump's mob try to tear our democracy apart with their bare hands. I held the line that day. I testified. I fought back with everything I had.**
And I'll be damned if I let dark money and MAGA intimidation knock me down.
I'm running for this district, for this state, and for the idea that our democracy is worth defending even when it's hard. Especially when it's hard.
That means standing up to Donald Trump. It means standing up to the billionaires and the PACs and the anonymous money that's quietly buying our elections out from under us.
_It means being exactly the kind of elected official that corporate donors are spending all that money to keep out._
[**But look, Peter, if I’m going to compete with the billionaires and come out on top, I need grassroots Democrats like you on my team. Folks,

**I'll give it to you straight — no hedging, no political doublespeak.**

My advisors just walked in with numbers I don't like ahead of our End-of-Quarter Deadline. We're losing ground financially, we're running into the red, and if we don't close this emergency fundraising deadline, this campaign takes a serious hit.

I've fought in Afghanistan. I've stared down bad odds before. But this fight — right here — requires reinforcements from people like you.

Thomas R. Donovan standing at the Chicago Board of Trade. (Exclusive photo courtesy of the Donovan family)
By Mark Vargas, Editor-in-Chief

Thomas R. Donovan, the longtime aide to legendary Chicago Mayor Richard J. Daley, former president and chief executive officer of the Chicago Board of Trade, has passed away, closing the chapter on one of the last remaining figures closely identified with the original Chicago political machine.

For decades, Donovan occupied a unique place in Chicago history, serving both as one of the principal operators inside Daley’s City Hall and later as a respected leader in the city’s business community.

Today he will be laid to rest.

subject: Happy Freedom Day!

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_med_email-26q2?refcode=x_260619_Juneteenth_act [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_med_email-26q2?refcode=x_260619_Juneteenth_act]
Today marks the 161st anniversary of Juneteenth, the day the remaining enslaved Americans in Texas learned of their freedom, two years after the Emancipation Proclamation.
On Juneteenth, we celebrate the Americans who fought—and continue to fight—to ensure our nation lives up to its founding promise that all people are created equal.
We are also reminded that progress is never guaranteed. Every generation is called upon to protect and expand the freedoms won by those who came before us and remember, celebrate, and honor our history. We must all work together to stop those in power from erasing American history, Black history, our history—and our voices.
As we honor Freedom Day, we recommit ourselves to the powerful work of building a country where everyone has an equal voice, equal opportunity, and equal protection under the law.
This year, Donald Trump’s SCOTUS ruling in Louisiana v. Callais further dismantled the Voting Rights Act and allowed for discriminatory practices to disempower voters across the country. It’s a racist, anti-democratic ruling, and one I will fight every day.
Together, we can build a country where life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness are not reserved for a privileged few but are rights enjoyed by all. I hope you will join me.
Happy Juneteenth. May we honor the past, celebrate the progress we've made, and continue the work of creating a more perfect union.
Stay Loud,
Maxine
