name: Lizzie Fletcher
subject: This Juneteenth
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS
body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Non-Re-Elect%20Logo.png]
Today, we celebrate Juneteenth and all it represents, in Texas and across the country.
Juneteenth has special significance for Texans because on this day in 1865—more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation was issued—Texans received word of the end of slavery in the U.S. when Major General Gordon Granger arrived in Galveston and announced that all slaves were now free and had “absolute equality” of personal rights and property rights. That moment marked a turning point in our nation's long and unfinished journey toward freedom, equality, and justice.
Since that day, Texans have recognized Juneteenth as a celebration of freedom, of progress, and of hope that guides us forward. It is a moment to honor the courage and perseverance of those who have fought for freedom and justice before us and to commit ourselves to that cause today.
But this Juneteenth arrives at a moment when our history is under a deliberate and unyielding attack—even from those who have sworn an oath to protect it. Over the last year and half, we have witnessed a campaign from our own White House to erase much of the history of the United States and the people who made it. And it isn’t stopping. As we approach America’s 250th year, it’s more important than ever to tell the full, deep, complex stories of these United States.
The history of the United States is deep and complicated—from its inspiring and transformational founding to the progress that followed and the failures to to extend that progress to all Americans along the way. We should be proud of the progress we have made—and equally aware of the work we still need to make. And that starts with understanding our history. All of it. Seeking a full and honest accounting of our past helps continue the work to live up to our founding ideals of freedom and justice for all.
Juneteenth is a celebration of our ability to do that—to advance the cause of freedom, to make meaningful progress, and to maintain our faith in the promise and the people of this country. That’s why the celebration of Juneteenth—and the celebration of the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence just a few weeks from now—is so very powerful and important. We are reminded that it is the people who have advanced our freedom—fighting for it, expanding it, cherishing it, and believing it in and all it enables—and who are the ones who have written our history.
Every generation is called upon to defend and expand the freedoms secured by those who came before it. And the call today is loud. As we celebrate freedom and progress and hope, we must also protect them. It is our job to protect our progress and the promise of America. And I’ll be there beside you in the work.
Together we can do anything,
Lizzie Signature [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/lizzie_signature-1.png]

America’s border security is finally being reinforced instead of weakened.

For years, our border was overwhelmed. Agents were outnumbered. Cartels exploited the chaos. And communities across the country paid the price.

Now enforcement is being strengthened—but it only works if Americans stand behind it.

Friend,
Juneteenth reminds us that freedom, equality, and democracy don't happen on their own. They require people willing to keep pushing our country forward.
Colorado's history is filled with examples of that determination. Formerly enslaved pioneers like Clara Brown, Barney Ford, Julia Greeley, James Beckwourth, and Isom Dart helped build communities across our state. They were entrepreneurs, civic leaders, explorers, ranchers, and advocates who overcame enormous obstacles to leave a lasting mark on Colorado.
Their stories are a reminder that Colorado has always been strengthened by people whose voices were too often ignored but who refused to be left out of the American story.
As we reflect on Juneteenth, we honor those who expanded the promise of freedom and helped build a more inclusive democracy.
That spirit guides our campaign.
Colorado's 3rd District is full of people from different backgrounds, communities, and walks of life. Our campaign is rooted in the belief that every voice matters, every community deserves to be heard, and our democracy is strongest when everyone has a seat at the table.
I will always fight for the equity of opportunity.
Happy Juneteenth.
Alex Kelloff

In 2021, I supported legislation to make Juneteenth a federal holiday. Still, many Americans do not know the true history of emancipation, and right now, the Trump administration is trying to keep it that way. Across the nation, MAGA is trying to rewrite history by attacking history curriculum in public schools and cutting funding to African American heritage sites and federal research and grants that mention enslavement. **That’s why it is so important that you and I share the truth of what happened in the past, and take time to honor that in the present.** I hope you’ll join me in doing so, whether at a joyous Juneteenth celebration or by having a reflective conversation with those around you about what Juneteenth represents. clean_body: | | | Friends, Today is Juneteenth, a holiday that commemorates June 19th, 1865, when all enslaved people were legally freed, nearly two years after the Emancipation Proclamation was signed. Today and always, we remember the inspiring strength and courage that the African American community showed under the dehumanizing, life-threatening conditions that were forced upon them under chattel slavery. We also remember the countless African Americans who fought for and supported the Union, but were still denied freedom by the United States. In 2021, I supported legislation to make Juneteenth a federal holiday. Still, many Americans do not know the true history of emancipation, and right now, the Trump administration is trying to keep it that way. Across the nation, MAGA is trying to rewrite history by attacking history curriculum in public schools and cutting funding to African American heritage sites and federal research and grants that mention enslavement. That’s why it is so important that you and I share the truth of what happened in the past, and take time to honor that in the present. I hope you’ll join me in doing so, whether at a joyous Juneteenth celebration or by having a reflective conversation with those around you about what Juneteenth represents. Happy Juneteenth, Doris Matsui As a Member of Congress, Doris works to ensure that the voices of her district’s constituents are heard in Congress, and fights for the needs of the Sacramento region. body:
https://www.jenaforcolorado.com/ [https://www.jenaforcolorado.com/]
Happy Juneteenth, Peter.
Today, we celebrate the day enslaved Black Americans in Texas, finally gained their freedom, more than two years after President Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation.
As we commemorate their freedom, we must also remember that the struggle for equality continues. Across the country, Black voters still face attacks on their fundamental rights and efforts to diminish their voices.
Juneteenth is about remembering our history and reflecting on the values that define us and the future we want to build together. I believe America is strongest when everyone has a fair shot, every voice is valued, and the law protects all people equally.
On this day of remembrance and reflection, I’m honoring the courage, resilience, and contributions of generations who fought for freedom. As Colorado’s Secretary of State and as a candidate for Attorney General, I am renewing my commitment to the work of justice that continues today.
Happy Juneteenth.
— Jena

August 8, 2009, is a date I will never forget.
Just days before his 19th birthday, my son Justin was out in the fields with us, doing what this family has done for over three generations—farming the Louisiana delta. A breakdown in our combine left corn spilled across the ground, and as we worked to recover it, Justin got too close. In an instant, his pant leg was caught, and the thresher pulled him in.
I can still hear his voice: “Dad, get me out.”
And there was nothing I could do.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
Multiple miracles occurred that day: When it initially happened he wasn’t in pain because his nerves were pinched so tightly in the machine. Nor was he bleeding because he was caught so tight in there.
It took the jaws of life to tear apart that machine and when the metal finally gave way he let out a scream that I will never forget for the rest of my life.
The paramedics quickly sprang into action and he was airlifted to Jackson, Mississippi, where Doctors fought to save his leg, but the injury and infection from all the dirt and debris were too severe. Justin lost his leg from below the knee.
That day could have broken us. Instead, it showed me what makes Louisiana strong.
Neighbors, first responders from two parishes (what we call counties in Louisiana), and a doctor who wasn’t even on duty, Dr. Ron Gregg, a farmer himself and longtime family friend — showed up because that’s what rural communities do. They take care of each other. They don’t ask if it’s their job or jurisdiction. They just show up.
Today, Justin is 35. He runs our farm. He’s built a life, with a fiancée and a family of his own. He still hunts, fishes, and works the land — just with a prosthetic leg and the same determination that carried him through that day.
But the truth is, the kind of community that saved Justin is disappearing. Rural hospitals are closing. Doctors like Dr. Gregg—who live in our communities, who know our families—are harder to find. Too many of our kids feel like they have to leave home to build a future.
And my family, who first worked this Louisiana delta soil as slaves and sharecroppers, and now as farmers who own this land, have put too much blood into this soil for us to leave and go somewhere else.
I have to take a stand and fight for our way of life and it’s why I am proud to be the Democrat running for Senate in Louisiana.
If you believe in that fight, I’m asking you to stand with me today. A Democratic win here is the first step in taking our state back from the far-right whose policies of atomization and vicious corporatism are tearing our communities apart.
And mark my words, a win is possible, Democrats just won a deep red special election here by a landslide. The blue wave will wash over Louisiana and we will flip this seat but only if we fight for it. Will you please make a contribution of $50, $20, or even just $10 to help us in our fight to restore the Louisiana that we love so dearly. Thank you. Your support means more than you know.

Louisiana
